definition_zh: 年龄；年岁；老年；时代；时期；变老；陈化
definition_en: the number of years a person or thing has lived, or a long period in history
core_image: 树干上一圈圈年轮，把流走的时间刻成了可以数出的痕迹
scene: 老木匠抚摸着院里的老榆树，一圈一圈数着树干上的年轮。Each ring on the trunk marked an age of slow growth.
sceneCN: 这里 age 是「年龄、年岁」（第 1 个义项：人或物存在的时间长度）；句意为树干上的每一圈年轮都标记着一段缓慢生长的岁月。图中可辨识物件：老榆树、年轮、木匠的手。

pos.zh: 名词：年龄；年岁；老年；时代；时期
动词：变老；使显老；陈化

derivatives.zh: 由 age 加 -ed 构成，义为「年老的；陈年的」
由 age 加 -less 构成，义为「不显老的；永恒的」
由 age 加 -ing 构成，义为「老化；变老的过程」
由 age 加 -ism 构成，义为「年龄歧视」

senses.title: The number of years lived
senses.definition: the number of years that a person or thing has lived or existed
senses.definitionCN: 人或物已经生存或存在的年数
senses.example: She started learning the piano at the age of six.
senses.exampleCN: 她六岁开始学钢琴。
senses.why: Latin aetas, from aevum 'lifetime', counted the span a person or thing had lived; the noun began as that number.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 aetas 出自 aevum「一生」，用来计算人或物已活过的跨度；名词最初就是这个数字。

senses.title: The later part of life
senses.definition: the state of being old, or the late period of a person's life
senses.definitionCN: 年老的状态，或一个人生命的晚期
senses.example: His hands showed the marks of age, but his eyes were still bright.
senses.exampleCN: 他的双手留下岁月的痕迹，眼睛却依然明亮。
senses.why: The same span, seen from its end, turns from a count of years into the condition of having many of them.
senses.whyCN: 同一段时间跨度从末端看，就从「年数的计数」转为「年数很多的状态」。

senses.title: A historical period
senses.definition: a particular period of history, often named after its dominant technology or culture
senses.definitionCN: 历史上某个特定时期，常以其主导的技术或文化命名
senses.example: The Bronze Age followed the Stone Age in many parts of the world.
senses.exampleCN: 在世界许多地方，青铜时代紧接石器时代而来。
senses.why: Aetas also named a long stretch of the world's life, so the word widened from one person's years to a whole era.
senses.whyCN: aetas 也指世界存续的一大段时光，于是词义从一个人的年岁扩展到整个时代。

senses.title: A stage in development
senses.definition: a distinct period in the development of something, such as an industry or an idea
senses.definitionCN: 事物发展过程中的一个明显阶段，如某个行业或某种观念
senses.example: The company has entered a new age of digital trade.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司已进入数字贸易的新时期。
senses.why: Institutions are pictured as living things; if they live, they too pass through ages.
senses.whyCN: 机构被比作有生命的东西；既然有生命，它们也会经历一个个时期。

senses.title: To grow old
senses.definition: to become older, or to show the effects of passing years
senses.definitionCN: 变老，或显出岁月流逝的影响
senses.example: He has aged a great deal since the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 事故之后他老了很多。
senses.why: The noun became a verb: to age is to undergo what the noun measures.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词：age 就是经历名词所计量的那件事。

senses.title: To make someone look old
senses.definition: to cause a person to look older than they are, usually through worry or hardship
senses.definitionCN: 使人看起来比实际年龄更老，常因忧虑或艰辛所致
senses.example: Years of worry had aged her beyond her years.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的忧虑使她显得比实际年龄苍老。
senses.why: The verb takes a causative turn: time does its work on someone, and the speaker names the result.
senses.whyCN: 动词带上使役色彩：时间在某人身上起作用，说话人则点明结果。

senses.title: To mature with time
senses.definition: to be left for a period so that flavor, texture, or quality improves
senses.definitionCN: 放置一段时间，使风味、质地或品质变得更好
senses.example: The cheese is left to age for two years in a cool cellar.
senses.exampleCN: 这种奶酪要在阴凉的地窖里陈化两年。
senses.why: Here time is a craftsman: the object is not merely getting older but being improved by the wait.
senses.whyCN: 这里时间是工匠：对象不只是变旧，而是在等待中被改良。

intro.en: Age goes back through Old French to Latin aetas, a word for a lifetime that also came to name whole eras.
intro.cn: age 经由古法语上溯到拉丁语 aetas，这个词本指一生，后来也用来指整个时代。

items.en: *aiw- is reconstructed as 'vital force, life, long time', the root behind words for age and eternity.
items.cn: 原始印欧语 *aiw- 被重构为「生命力、生命、长久」，是表示年龄与永恒的词根。

items.en: Aevum meant a span of time or a lifetime, and aetas, from the same family, meant age or a stage of life.
items.cn: aevum 意为「一段时间、一生」，同族的 aetas 意为「年岁、人生的阶段」。

items.en: Old French aage, derived from aetas, named both a person's years and a historical period.
items.cn: 古法语 aage 出自 aetas，既指人的年岁，也指历史上的一段时期。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the thirteenth century and kept the personal and the historical senses together.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入这个词，人的年岁与历史时期两种含义一并保留。

items.en: The verb grew out of the noun, and compounds such as middle-aged and teenage spread the idea of a measured span.
items.cn: 动词用法由名词生长出来，middle-aged、teenage 等复合词把「可度量的时间跨度」这一观念扩散开来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same root; the near-meaning group gathers time words of different length.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词根构成的一族词；近义组收表示不同长度时间的词。

entries.definition: An adjective describing someone or something that is old or has been left to mature.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「年老的；陈化的」，指人或物年纪大或经过陈放。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning never seeming to grow old or never ending.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不显老的；永恒的」，指似乎不会变老或没有终点。

entries.definition: The noun or adjective for the process of growing older.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「老化；变老的」，指逐渐年长的过程。

entries.definition: A long and distinct period of history named for its character or events.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「时代；纪元」，指以特征或事件命名的漫长历史时期。

entries.definition: A period marked by a memorable event or a new stage of development.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「纪元；新时代」，指以重大事件或新发展阶段为标志的时期。

entries.definition: A length of time defined by particular features or events.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「时期；阶段」，指具有特定特征或事件的一段时间。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the word to rings, candles and the look of the letters.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个记忆钩子把这个词与年轮、蜡烛以及字母外形联系起来。

normal.en: Think of tree rings: one ring for each year of age.
normal.cn: 想到树的年轮：每长一岁就多一圈。

normal.en: Picture a birthday cake with candles, one for every year of age.
normal.cn: 想象插着蜡烛的生日蛋糕，每一根代表一岁。

normal.en: AGE begins with the same letters as 'A Great Era'.
normal.cn: age 的开头字母可以读成「A Great Era」，暗示一段伟大的时期。

normal.en: Link age with aged: both describe what long years do to a person.
normal.cn: 把 age 与 aged 连在一起记：两者都描述漫长岁月在人身上留下的痕迹。

normal.en: The word hides 'a generation': age is a generation measured in years.
normal.cn: 这个词里藏着「a generation」的影子：年龄就是以年为单位量出的一代时光。

abstract.en: Age is time made visible: rings, wrinkles and dates all count it.
abstract.cn: 年龄是看得见的时间：年轮、皱纹与日期都在为它计数。

abstract.en: From one life span the word stretches out to whole civilizations.
abstract.cn: 从一个生命的长度出发，这个词延伸到了整个文明。

abstract.en: To age is to let time do its slow work, whether on a body or on cheese.
abstract.cn: 变老就是让时间慢慢做功，无论作用在身体还是在奶酪上。

examples.en: At the age of thirty, she changed careers completely.
examples.cn: 三十岁时，她彻底换了行业。

examples.en: He has aged gracefully, still walking five kilometers every morning.
examples.cn: 他老得很从容，每天早晨仍走五公里。

examples.en: The wine needs time to age before it is bottled.
examples.cn: 这酒在装瓶前需要时间陈化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「诶，这」：诶，这老人多大岁数了？说的就是年龄。

root: 拉丁语 aetas（年岁、一生）与 aevum（漫长的时间）同源，原始印欧语 *aiw- 表示「生命力、长久」，由「一生的长度」引申出「年龄」与「时代」。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts from a counted life span, then widens to historical periods and to the process of growing or maturing.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从可计数的一生长度出发，进而扩展到历史时期，以及变老、陈化的过程。

branches.en: the measured length of life
the late part of that span
a span widened to history or to a stage
branches.cn: 扩展到历史或发展阶段的跨度

branches.en: time working on a body
time working for quality

intro.en: Age is a free-standing word, but it joins freely with suffixes and with other nouns to name people and periods.
intro.cn: age 是独立成词的词，但它能自由地接后缀、也能与其他名词组合，用来指人和时期。

latinIntro.en: Its Latin family gathers around aevum and aetas, the words for a lifetime and for an era.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词族围绕 aevum 与 aetas，也就是表示「一生」与「时代」的两个词。

items.meaning: having lived many years, or having been left to mature
items.example: The aged farmer still works in the fields.
items.exampleCN: 年迈的农夫仍在田里劳作。

items.meaning: never seeming to grow old, or never coming to an end
items.example: Her face seemed ageless in the soft light.
items.exampleCN: 柔和的光线下，她的面容似乎永不衰老。

items.example: Aging is a natural part of every life.
items.exampleCN: 变老是一切生命自然的一部分。

items.meaning: unfair treatment of people because of their age
items.example: Ageism can cost experienced workers their jobs.
items.exampleCN: 年龄歧视可能让经验丰富的工人失去工作。

items.example: The middle-aged man took up running last spring.
items.exampleCN: 那位中年男子去年春天开始跑步。

items.meaning: relating to people from thirteen to nineteen years old
items.example: She writes novels for teenage readers.
items.exampleCN: 她为青少年读者写小说。

items.meaning: existing for a very long time
items.example: The two villages settled an age-old dispute at last.
items.exampleCN: 两个村子终于解决了由来已久的争端。

items.meaning: younger than the age required by law
items.meaningCN: 未成年的；未达法定年龄的
items.example: The club refuses entry to underage visitors.
items.exampleCN: 这家俱乐部拒绝未达年龄的来客入内。

items.meaning: older than the age allowed for a purpose
items.example: The team had to drop its overage players.
items.exampleCN: 球队不得不放弃超龄球员。

latinEntries.meaning: a lifetime, a long span of time, eternity

latinEntries.structure: from aevum, with the -t- noun suffix
latinEntries.meaning: age, a stage of life, a period of history
latinEntries.meaningCN: 年岁；人生阶段；历史时期

definition_zh: 代理机构；经销处；（政府）机构；代理关系；能动性；作用
definition_en: a business or organization that acts for others, or the power to act and produce effects
core_image: 把事务交到一只可靠的手里，让它替你出面办理
scene: 旅行社的柜台前排着长队，工作人员正替客人预订远行的机票。The travel agency handled every booking, visa and hotel for the group.
sceneCN: 这里 agency 是「代理机构」（第 1 个义项：代他人办理事务的商业机构）；句意为这家旅行社替整个团队办妥了订票、签证与酒店。图中可辨识物件：柜台、机票、行李箱。

pos.zh: 名词：代理机构；经销处；政府机构；能动性

collocations.zh: 通过……的作用；经由……的中介

derivatives.zh: 由 ag- 加 -ent 构成，义为「代理人；行为者」
由 agent 加 -ial 构成，义为「代理的；行为者的」
由 sub- 加 agency 构成，义为「分代理处；支机构」

senses.title: A business that acts for clients
senses.definition: a company that provides a service by acting on behalf of its clients, such as a travel or advertising agency
senses.definitionCN: 代客户办理事务以提供服务的公司，如旅行社或广告公司
senses.example: The travel agency booked our flights and hotels.
senses.exampleCN: 这家旅行社替我们订好了机票和酒店。
senses.why: Latin agere meant to do; an agency is a business whose whole work is doing things for other people.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 agere 意为「做」；代理机构就是一家专门替别人办事的公司。

senses.title: A public body of the state
senses.definition: an official organization, usually part of a government, that administers a public service or regulation
senses.definitionCN: 通常隶属于政府的官方机构，负责管理某项公共服务或规章
senses.example: A government agency is investigating the river pollution.
senses.exampleCN: 一个政府机构正在调查这条河的污染。
senses.why: The state acts through bodies of its own; each such body is the state's agent, hence its agency.
senses.whyCN: 国家通过自身的机构行事；每个机构都是国家的代理人，所以称为 agency。

senses.title: The relation of acting for another
senses.definition: the legal relationship in which one person is authorized to act on behalf of another
senses.definitionCN: 一方获授权代表另一方行事的法律关系
senses.example: The agency agreement allows him to sign contracts for the company.
senses.exampleCN: 这份代理协议允许他代表公司签署合同。
senses.why: Here the word names not the office but the tie itself: the authority to do another's business.
senses.whyCN: 这里指的不是机构，而是关系本身：替他人办事的那份授权。

senses.title: The capacity to act
senses.titleCN: 能动性；自主行动的能力
senses.definition: the inner power of a person or group to act independently and make choices
senses.definitionCN: 个人或群体独立行动、作出选择的内在力量
senses.example: Children need room to develop their own agency.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子需要空间来发展自己的能动性。
senses.why: From an office full of agents the word abstracted the bare power of acting, a sense central to social science.
senses.whyCN: 从满是代理人的机构出发，这个词抽象出了纯粹的「行动能力」，这是社会科学的核心概念。

senses.title: The force that brings about an effect
senses.definition: the means or influence through which something is done or an effect is produced
senses.definitionCN: 完成某事或产生某种效果所凭借的手段或影响
senses.example: The reform succeeded through the agency of a few determined teachers.
senses.exampleCN: 这场改革借助几位坚定教师的力量取得了成功。
senses.why: If an agent is what does a thing, then agency can also mean the working of that force.
senses.whyCN: 既然 agent 是做事的那一方，agency 也就可以指那股力量的作用。

senses.title: A local branch of a service
senses.definition: a local office or branch through which a larger organization serves a district
senses.definitionCN: 较大的机构在某一地区设立、用来服务当地的办事处
senses.example: The bank opened a small agency in the mountain town.
senses.exampleCN: 这家银行在山中小镇开设了一个代理处。
senses.why: A branch is the parent organization acting at a distance, a piece of the agency placed in one place.
senses.whyCN: 分支机构就是母机构在远处的行动，是代理机构安放在某一处的一块。

intro.en: Agency comes from the Latin verb 'to do', through the noun for an agent's office.
intro.cn: agency 出自拉丁语表示「做」的动词，经由表示「代理人事务」的名词而来。

items.en: Agere meant to do, drive, or set in motion; its present participle agens named the one who acts.
items.cn: agere 意为「做、驱动、使运动」；其现在分词 agens 指「行动的人」。

items.en: Agentia named the office or function of an agent, the business of doing something for another.
items.cn: agentia 指代理人的职务或职能，即替他人办事这件事。

items.en: Old French agence carried the commercial sense of an office that acts for clients.
items.cn: 古法语 agence 带有「替客户办事的机构」这一商业含义。

items.en: English adopted agency for a place or person acting on behalf of another, first in trade and law.
items.cn: 英语借入 agency，用来指代他人行事的地方或人，最早见于商业与法律。

items.en: Political and social writing added the abstract sense of capacity to act, now familiar as human agency.
items.cn: 政治与社会学写作又增添了「行动能力」这一抽象义，如今常见于「人的能动性」这一说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same acting root; the near-meaning group gathers kinds of organizations.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「行动」词根的一族词；近义组收不同类型的组织。

entries.definition: A person who acts for another, especially in business or law.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「代理人；经纪人」，指替他人行事的人，尤见于商业或法律。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning relating to an agent or to the power of acting.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「代理的；与行动能力有关的」。

entries.definition: A list of things to be done or discussed at a meeting.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「议程；待办事项」，与 agency 词形相近但来源不同。

entries.definition: An office or department, often a government one, that handles a particular service.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「局；办事处」，常指负责某项服务的政府机构。

entries.definition: A business company, especially one providing professional services.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「公司；事务所」，尤指提供专业服务的商号。

entries.definition: An established organization such as a bank, school, or hospital.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「机构；制度」，指银行、学校、医院等已设立的组织。

normalIntro.en: These hooks connect the word to agents, travel desks and the ending that names an office.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个记忆钩子把这个词与代理人、旅行社柜台以及表示机构的词尾联系起来。

normal.en: AGENCY contains agent: an agency is where agents work.
normal.cn: agency 里面藏着 agent：代理机构就是代理人工作的地方。

normal.en: Think of a travel agency that acts for you when you cannot go yourself.
normal.cn: 想想旅行社：你自己去不了时，它替你跑腿。

normal.en: The ending -cy turns agent into the place or business of agents.
normal.cn: 词尾 -cy 把 agent 变成代理人所在的场所或买卖。

normal.en: Break it into a-gen-cy and hear 'an agent sees to it'.
normal.cn: 拆成 a-gen-cy，听起来像「an agent sees to it」，即一位代理人在照看这件事。

normal.en: A government agency is a public body that acts for the state.
normal.cn: 政府机构就是代国家行事的公共部门。

abstract.en: Agency is action that has been handed to someone trusted.
abstract.cn: 代理就是把行动交到可信的人手里。

abstract.en: The word moves from a building full of agents to the bare power to act.
abstract.cn: 这个词从一屋子代理人，走到赤裸裸的行动能力。

abstract.en: When people speak of human agency, they mean the will to change things.
abstract.cn: 人们谈人的能动性时，说的是改变事物的意志。

examples.en: The travel agency arranged everything, from visas to airport pickup.
examples.cn: 旅行社把一切安排妥当，从签证到接机。

examples.en: She felt she had no agency in the decision that changed her life.
examples.cn: 在那项改变她人生的决定里，她觉得自己毫无主动权。

examples.en: Through the agency of a mutual friend, the two rivals finally met.
examples.cn: 在一位共同朋友的中介下，两位对手终于见了面。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「诶，真细」：诶，真细致，代理机构把每件事都替你办妥了。

root: 拉丁语 agere（做、驱动）的现在分词 agens 指「做事的人」，加 -tia 构成 agentia「代理的事务」，再经古法语 agence 进入英语，核心是「替他人行事」。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins with a business that acts for clients, spreads to public bodies and legal ties, and ends with abstract power and local branches.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从替客户办事的商业机构开始，扩展到政府机构与法律关系，最后落在抽象的行动能力与地方分支上。

core.en: THE POWER TO ACT FOR ANOTHER

branches.en: a business or branch that acts for clients
branches.cn: 替客户办事的机构或分支

branches.en: a public body acting for the state

intro.en: Agency belongs to the large family of ag- words, all built on the Latin verb for doing and driving.
intro.cn: agency 属于庞大的 ag- 词族，这一族都建立在拉丁语表示「做与驱动」的动词上。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base ag- produces agent, agenda, act and agile, each naming a different face of action.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词基 ag- 生出 agent、agenda、act、agile，各自呈现行动的一个侧面。

items.meaning: one who acts, or one who acts for another
items.example: The agent signed the contract for the singer.
items.exampleCN: 代理人替这位歌手签了合同。

items.meaning: relating to an agent or to agency
items.meaningCN: 代理的；与行动者有关的
items.example: The report stressed the agential role of local leaders.
items.exampleCN: 报告强调了地方领导者的能动作用。

items.meaning: a secondary agent who works under another
items.example: Each subagent reports to the main agent.
items.exampleCN: 每位副代理人都向主代理人汇报。

items.meaning: a branch agency under a larger one
items.example: The insurer opened a subagency in the county.
items.exampleCN: 这家保险公司在该县开设了一个分代理处。

items.example: The agency-wide review begins next month.
items.exampleCN: 全机构范围的审查下个月开始。

items.meaning: naming the doer of an action
items.example: The suffix -er is agentive in teacher.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 在 teacher 中表示施动者。

items.meaning: someone free to act or sign independently
items.example: After the season, he became a free agent.
items.exampleCN: 赛季结束后，他成了自由球员。

items.meaning: a publicist who handles publicity for a client
items.example: Her press agent arranged the interviews.
items.exampleCN: 她的宣传代理人安排了采访。

items.meaning: a business that arranges trips for clients
items.example: The travel agency found us a cheap flight.
items.exampleCN: 旅行社替我们找到了一班便宜航班。

definition_zh: 议程；待办事项清单；政治议题；隐秘意图
definition_en: a list of matters to be discussed or done, especially at a meeting
core_image: 一张写满待办事项的清单，摆在会议桌的最前面
scene: 会议开始前，秘书把印好的清单放在每位参会者面前。The first item on the agenda was the city budget.
sceneCN: 这里 agenda 是「议程」（第 1 个义项：会议要讨论事项的清单）；句意为议程上的第一项是城市预算。图中可辨识物件：会议桌、打印清单、文件夹。

pos.zh: 名词：议程；待办事项；政治议题

derivatives.zh: agenda 的拉丁语单数形式，义为「单件待办事项」
由 agenda 加 setting 构成的复合词，义为「议程设置」

senses.title: A list for a meeting
senses.definition: a list of the items to be discussed at a meeting, usually in a fixed order
senses.definitionCN: 会议上要讨论的事项清单，通常按固定顺序排列
senses.example: The first item on the agenda was the city budget.
senses.exampleCN: 议程上的第一项是城市预算。
senses.why: Latin agenda is the neuter plural of the future participle of agere, literally 'things to be done'; a meeting list is exactly that.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 agenda 是 agere 将来分词的中性复数，字面就是「该做的事」；会议清单正是这个意思。

senses.title: A personal list of tasks
senses.definition: a private list of things that a person intends to do, often kept as a reminder
senses.definitionCN: 个人打算完成的事项清单，常留作提醒
senses.example: He kept a short agenda of tasks beside his desk.
senses.exampleCN: 他在桌旁放着一张简短的待办清单。
senses.why: The 'things to be done' need not belong to a meeting; anyone can write down what must be done next.
senses.whyCN: 「该做的事」不必属于会议；任何人都可以写下接下来必须做的事。

senses.title: The issues a group pushes
senses.definition: the set of issues that a government, party, or organization treats as important
senses.definitionCN: 政府、政党或组织视为重要的议题集合
senses.example: Climate change is now high on the political agenda.
senses.exampleCN: 气候变化如今在政治议题中占据重要位置。
senses.why: A political body also works from a list of what it means to do; that list becomes its public agenda.
senses.whyCN: 政治团体同样按一份「打算做什么」的清单行事；这份清单就成了它公开的议程。

senses.title: A concealed intention
senses.titleCN: 隐秘意图；不可告人的目的
senses.definition: a hidden motive or plan behind an action that appears innocent
senses.definitionCN: 表面无害的行为背后隐藏的动机或计划
senses.example: The committee suspected a hidden agenda behind the generous offer.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会怀疑这份慷慨提议背后另有隐秘意图。
senses.why: If there is an open agenda, there can be a hidden one: a list of things to be done that is kept out of sight.
senses.whyCN: 既然有公开的议程，就可能有隐藏的议程：一份不让人看见的待办清单。

senses.title: A programme of action
senses.definition: a planned programme of measures that an organization intends to carry out
senses.definitionCN: 某组织打算实施的一整套措施计划
senses.example: The party published its agenda for reform in the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 该党在春天公布了改革纲领。
senses.why: The list of things to be done grows into a full programme when the doer is a large organization.
senses.whyCN: 当行动者是庞大的组织时，这份待办清单就会长成一套完整的纲领。

senses.title: The printed meeting document
senses.definition: the printed booklet or sheet that lists the order of business for a meeting
senses.definitionCN: 列出会议事务顺序的印刷册页或单页
senses.example: Delegates received the agenda two days before the summit.
senses.exampleCN: 代表们在峰会前两天收到了议程册。
senses.why: Here the abstract list takes physical form: the paper that participants hold in their hands.
senses.whyCN: 这里抽象的清单有了实体形态：参会者手里拿着的那张纸。

intro.en: Agenda is Latin for 'things to be done', a plural participle that English borrowed whole.
intro.cn: agenda 是拉丁语「该做的事」，一个复数分词形式被英语整体借入。

items.en: Agere meant to do, drive, or set in motion, the source of a large family of action words.
items.cn: agere 意为「做、驱动、使运动」，是一大批行动类词语的源头。

items.en: Agenda is the neuter plural of the future passive participle, so it means 'the things that must be done'.
items.cn: agenda 是将来被动分词的中性复数，因此意为「必须被做的事」。

items.en: The word was used for the list of items in a church service, an early written agenda.
items.cn: 这个词曾用于指教堂礼拜程序清单，是较早的成文议程。

items.en: English borrowed agenda as a list of matters to be attended to, first in religious and official use.
items.cn: 英语借入 agenda，指需要处理的事项清单，最早用于宗教与公务场合。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word widened to the political programme a group intends to carry out.
items.cn: 二十世纪时，词义扩展到某团体打算推行的政治纲领。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same doing root; the near-meaning group gathers lists and plans of events.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「做」词根的一族词；近义组收各种清单与日程安排。

entries.definition: A person who acts for another, especially in business or law.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「代理人」，指替他人行事的人，尤见于商业或法律。

entries.definition: A business or organization that acts on behalf of others.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「代理机构」，指代他人行事的商业或公共组织。

entries.definition: The rare singular of agenda, meaning a single item to be done.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，agenda 的罕见单数形式，义为「单件待办事项」。

entries.definition: A plan that lists times at which events are to happen.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「日程表；时间表」，列出事件发生的时间。

entries.definition: A chart showing the times of classes, trains, or other events.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「时刻表；课程表」，标出课程、列车等的时间。

entries.definition: A planned series of events or actions with a stated purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「计划；节目单」，指有既定目的一系列活动。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the word to meeting lists, Latin participles and the idea of things still to be done.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个记忆钩子把这个词与会议清单、拉丁语分词以及「还没做的事」这一观念联系起来。

normal.en: AGENDA sounds like 'a gen da': a general list for the day.
normal.cn: agenda 读起来像「a gen da」，可以想成一天的总清单。

normal.en: Picture the printed list placed in front of every chair at a meeting.
normal.cn: 想象会议中每把椅子前都摆着一份打印清单。

normal.en: Agenda and agent share the same start: both are about doing things.
normal.cn: agenda 与 agent 开头相同：两者都与「做事」有关。

normal.en: The word literally means 'things to be done', so it always points forward.
normal.cn: 这个词字面就是「该做的事」，所以永远指向未来。

normal.en: Remember 'hidden agenda': a list kept in a pocket instead of on the table.
normal.cn: 记住 hidden agenda 这个说法：一份藏在口袋里而不是摆在桌上的清单。

abstract.en: An agenda is a promise about what will be done next.
abstract.cn: 议程就是关于接下来要做什么的一份承诺。

abstract.en: Whoever writes the list decides what the group will notice.
abstract.cn: 写清单的人，决定了这个群体将注意到什么。

abstract.en: A hidden agenda is a plan wearing the mask of an innocent request.
abstract.cn: 隐秘议程就是戴着无害请求面具的计划。

examples.en: The chair asked whether anyone wished to add an item to the agenda.
examples.cn: 主席询问是否有人想在议程上增加一项。

examples.en: Affordable housing is at the top of the mayor's agenda.
examples.cn: 可负担住房是市长议程上的首要事项。

examples.en: They agreed to meet, but each side brought its own agenda.
examples.cn: 他们同意会面，但双方各怀自己的盘算。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「额，真大」：额，这份议程真大，条目一页接一页。

sensesIntro.en: The word runs from a literal list of things to be done, through meeting lists and political priorities, to concealed intentions.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从字面的「待办之事」出发，经过会议清单与政治优先事项，最后落到隐藏的意图。

intro.cn: agenda 是借入的拉丁语分词，但它与 agent、agency、agile 同属 ag- 词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base ag- supplies verbs of doing and driving, from which nouns and adjectives are formed.

items.example: The agent closed the deal quickly.
items.exampleCN: 代理人很快谈成了这笔交易。

items.meaning: the office or business of an agent
items.example: The agency hired two new translators.
items.exampleCN: 这家代理机构聘用了两名新译员。

items.meaning: a single item to be done
items.example: Each agendum was debated for ten minutes.
items.exampleCN: 每一项待办事项都辩论了十分钟。

items.meaning: the power to decide what others discuss
items.meaningCN: 议程设置；决定他人讨论内容的权力
items.example: The report studied agenda-setting in local media.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告研究了地方媒体的议程设置。

items.meaning: one point on a meeting list
items.example: Budget reform was the last agenda item.
items.exampleCN: 预算改革是最后一项议程。

items.meaning: able to move or think quickly
items.example: The agile team changed plans overnight.
items.exampleCN: 这个灵活的团队一夜之间改了计划。

items.meaning: the quality of being quick and nimble
items.example: Her agility surprised the older players.
items.exampleCN: 她的敏捷让年长的球员吃了一惊。

items.meaning: to shake, stir up, or campaign actively

definition_zh: 代理人；经纪人；特工；动因；剂；施事者
definition_en: a person who acts for another, or a thing that produces an effect
core_image: 被派出去替主人办事的那双手
scene: 谈判室里，一位受雇的中间人替双方传递条件。The agent negotiated the deal on behalf of the singer.
sceneCN: 这里 agent 是「代理人」（第 1 个义项：受雇代他人办事的人）；句意为这位代理人代表歌手谈成了这笔交易。图中可辨识物件：谈判桌、合同、录音笔。

pos.zh: 名词：代理人；经纪人；特工；动因；剂

derivatives.zh: 由 agent 加 -cy 构成，义为「代理机构；代理业务」
由 agent 加 -ial 构成，义为「代理的；行为者的」
由 agent 加 -ive 构成，义为「施事的；表示施动者的」
由 sub- 加 agent 构成，义为「副代理人；分代理人」

senses.title: One who acts for another
senses.definition: a person who is employed to act on behalf of another person or company
senses.definitionCN: 受雇代表他人或公司行事的人
senses.example: The agent negotiated the deal on behalf of the singer.
senses.exampleCN: 这名代理人代表歌手谈成了这笔交易。
senses.why: Latin agens is 'the one doing'; an agent is simply the person who does the business that someone else cannot do in person.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 agens 就是「正在做事的人」；代理人不过是替别人去做那件本人无法亲自办的事。

senses.title: A secret operative
senses.definition: a person secretly employed by a government to gather information or carry out operations
senses.definitionCN: 受政府秘密雇用、负责搜集情报或执行任务的人
senses.example: The agent passed the files to headquarters at midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 这名特工在午夜把文件交给了总部。
senses.why: A spy is also someone acting for another power, but in secret; the neutral word hides the secrecy.
senses.whyCN: 间谍同样是替另一股势力行事的人，只是行事隐秘；这个中性词把秘密藏了起来。

senses.title: A cause of change
senses.definition: a person or force that brings about change or produces an effect
senses.definitionCN: 带来变化或产生效果的人或力量
senses.example: She was the agent of change in the old factory.
senses.exampleCN: 她是那家老厂里变革的推动者。
senses.why: If an agent does things, it can also be the doer behind an event, not only a hired representative.
senses.whyCN: 既然 agent 是做事的一方，它也可以指事件背后的推动者，而不只是受雇的代表。

senses.title: An active substance
senses.definition: a substance that produces a particular effect, especially in chemistry or medicine
senses.definitionCN: 产生特定效果的物质，尤用于化学或医学
senses.example: Soap is a cleansing agent that lifts grease from cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 肥皂是一种去污剂，能把油污从布上带走。
senses.why: Science extended the word from people to things: whatever produces an effect is treated as the doer.
senses.whyCN: 科学把这个词从人扩展到物：凡是能产生效果的，都被当成施动者。

senses.title: The doer in a sentence
senses.definition: the person or thing that performs the action of a verb in a sentence
senses.definitionCN: 句子中执行动词所表示动作的人或物
senses.example: In the sentence, the dog is the agent of the biting.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个句子里，狗是咬这个动作的施事者。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the word for the role of the doer, the participant that carries out the action.
senses.whyCN: 语法学借用了这个词来表示「执行者」的角色，即承担动作的那个成分。

senses.title: A local representative
senses.definition: a business or person that represents a company in a particular area
senses.definitionCN: 在某一地区代表某公司的商号或个人
senses.example: Our agent in Shanghai handles all orders from the east.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在上海的代理商处理东部地区的全部订单。
senses.why: An organization cannot be everywhere at once, so it places an agent wherever it needs a hand.
senses.whyCN: 组织无法同时出现在所有地方，于是它把代理人安放在需要人手的地方。

intro.en: Agent is the Latin participle for 'one who is doing', carried into English through French.
intro.cn: agent 是拉丁语中表示「正在做事的人」的分词，经由法语进入英语。

items.en: Agere meant to do, drive, or set in motion; it is the verb behind act, agenda and agile as well.
items.cn: agere 意为「做、驱动、使运动」，act、agenda、agile 等词也出自它。

items.en: The present participle agens, stem agent-, named the person in the middle of doing something.
items.cn: 现在分词 agens 的词干是 agent-，指正在做事的那个人。

items.en: Old French agent kept the sense of a person who acts, especially in legal and commercial matters.
items.cn: 古法语 agent 保留了「行事之人」的含义，尤用于法律与商业事务。

items.en: English adopted agent first for a deputy or representative, then for any active cause.
items.cn: 英语先把它用作「代表、副手」，随后扩展到任何起作用的动因。

items.en: Chemistry and grammar added the agent as a substance or the doer of a verb, widening the word far beyond people.
items.cn: 化学与语法又让 agent 分别指药剂和动词的执行者，使这个词远远超出人的范围。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same-root nouns and adjectives; the near-meaning group gathers people who act for others.
note.cn: 形近组收同根名词与形容词；近义组收替他人行事的人。

entries.definition: A business or organization that acts on behalf of others.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「代理机构」，指代他人行事的商业或公共组织。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning relating to an agent or to the power of acting.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「代理的；与行动能力有关的」。

entries.definition: An adjective describing a form that names the doer of an action.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「施事的」，用于说明某个形式表示动作的执行者。

entries.definition: A person chosen to speak or act for a group.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「代表」，指被选出替群体发言或行事的人。

entries.definition: A person who buys and sells goods or services for others.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「经纪人」，指替他人买卖货物或服务的人。

entries.definition: A person sent to represent others at a meeting or event.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「代表；使节」，指被派去代表他人出席会议或活动的人。

normalIntro.en: These hooks connect the word to deputised work, spies and the '-ent' ending that marks a person.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个记忆钩子把这个词与受托办事、特工以及表示「人」的词尾 -ent 联系起来。

normal.en: AGENT ends in -ent, the ending found in 'student' and 'resident': a person.
normal.cn: agent 以 -ent 结尾，student 与 resident 也用这个结尾，提示它指一个人。

normal.en: Picture an actor's agent: someone who does the talking so the actor can work.
normal.cn: 想象艺人的经纪人：他负责交涉，艺人才能专心工作。

normal.en: A travel agent acts for you; an agency is where such agents sit.
normal.cn: 旅行代理人替你办事；代理机构就是这些人办公的地方。

normal.en: Secret agent: the word stays neutral while the job stays hidden.
normal.cn: secret agent 这个说法里，词本身中性，工作却隐秘。

normal.en: Agent and agenda start alike because both come from the verb 'to do'.
normal.cn: agent 与 agenda 开头相同，因为两者都出自表示「做」的那个动词。

abstract.en: An agent is will carried out by another pair of hands.
abstract.cn: 代理人就是由另一双手去执行的意志。

abstract.en: The word slides easily from people to chemicals and to grammar.
abstract.cn: 这个词轻易地从人滑向化学药剂，再滑向语法。

abstract.en: Every agent stands in a gap where the principal cannot be present.
abstract.cn: 每一个代理人都站在委托人无法亲自到场的那道缝隙里。

examples.en: The agent showed us three houses before we chose one.
examples.cn: 经纪人带我们看了三套房子，我们才作出选择。

examples.en: A secret agent delivered the documents before dawn.
examples.cn: 一名特工在天亮前送出了文件。

examples.en: She acted as her sister's agent during the negotiations.
examples.cn: 谈判期间她担任姐姐的代理人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「诶，真特」：诶，这位代理人真特别，什么事都能替你办。

root: 拉丁语 agere（做、驱动）的现在分词 agens、词干 agent-，本义「正在做事的人」，经古法语进入英语，泛指替他人办事者，也指产生效果的动因或药剂。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts with a hired representative, then covers spies, causes of change, chemical substances, grammatical doers and local agents.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从受雇的代表开始，随后覆盖特工、变化的动因、化学药剂、语法施事者与地方代理。

branches.en: a hired or local representative
a hidden operative of the state

intro.en: Agent is the core member of the ag- family; most related words are formed by suffix or by adding a noun.
intro.cn: agent 是 ag- 词族的中心成员，相关词多由加后缀或加名词复合而成。

latinIntro.en: Latin agere supplies the base; agent- adds the person, -cy the office, -ive the quality.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 agere 提供词基；agent- 加上「人」，-cy 加出「机构」，-ive 加出「性质」。

items.meaning: the office or business of an agent
items.example: The agency hired two new translators.
items.exampleCN: 这家代理机构聘用了两名新译员。

items.meaning: relating to an agent or to agency

items.meaning: naming the doer of an action
items.example: The suffix -er is agentive in teacher.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 在 teacher 中表示施动者。

items.example: Each subagent reports to the main agent.
items.exampleCN: 每位副代理人都向主代理人汇报。

items.meaning: someone free to act or sign independently
items.example: After the season, he became a free agent.

items.meaning: a spy working for a government
items.example: The secret agent avoided the main streets.
items.exampleCN: 这名特工避开了主干道。

items.meaning: a person who arranges trips for clients
items.example: The travel agent found a direct flight.
items.exampleCN: 旅行代理人找到了一班直飞航班。

items.meaning: a person or force that drives reform
items.example: The young mayor became an agent of change.
items.exampleCN: 这位年轻市长成了变革的推动者。

definition_zh: 使恶化；加重；激怒；使恼火
definition_en: to make a problem, illness, or situation worse, or to annoy someone
core_image: 往已经沉重的担子上再压一块石头
scene: 病人的伤口还没愈合，他又执意下地干活。Lack of rest aggravated the injury in his knee.
sceneCN: 这里 aggravate 是「使恶化」（第 1 个义项：使问题或病情变得更严重）；句意为缺少休息使他的膝伤更加严重。图中可辨识物件：绷带、拐杖、病床。

pos.zh: 动词：使恶化；加重；激怒

derivatives.zh: 由 aggravate 加 -ion 构成，义为「加重；恶化；激怒」
由 aggravate 加 -ing 构成，义为「令人恼火的；使恶化的」
由 aggravate 加 -ed 构成，义为「加重的；被激怒的」

senses.title: To make a condition worse
senses.definition: to make an illness, injury, or bad situation more serious
senses.definitionCN: 使疾病、伤势或糟糕的局面变得更加严重
senses.example: Lack of rest aggravated the injury in his knee.
senses.exampleCN: 缺少休息使他的膝伤更加严重。
senses.why: Latin gravis meant heavy; adding ad- 'toward' made aggravare 'to add weight', so the word pictures a load made heavier.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 gravis 意为「沉重」；加上 ad-「朝向」构成 aggravare「加重」，词的画面就是一担更沉的负荷。

senses.title: To add to a burden
senses.definition: to increase the weight of a burden, cost, or difficulty that already exists
senses.definitionCN: 增加原有负担、成本或困难的分量
senses.example: The new tax aggravated the burden on small shops.
senses.exampleCN: 新税加重了小店铺的负担。
senses.why: The same image works for money and work: whatever is already heavy can be made heavier.
senses.whyCN: 同样的画面也适用于金钱与工作：本来沉重的东西还能再被压重。

senses.title: To provoke or annoy
senses.definition: to make someone angry or irritated, especially by repeated behavior
senses.definitionCN: 使人生气或烦躁，尤因反复出现的行为
senses.example: His endless questions aggravated the tired teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 他没完没了的问题让疲惫的老师很恼火。
senses.why: An added weight is also felt on the nerves; the word shifted from burdens on the body to burdens on the temper.
senses.whyCN: 加在身上的重量也会压在神经上；词义于是从身体的负担转到脾气的负担。

senses.title: To make a legal offence graver
senses.definition: to make an offence more serious in law, usually by an added circumstance such as a weapon
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上使罪行更严重，通常因使用武器等附加情节
senses.example: The theft was aggravated by the use of a weapon.
senses.exampleCN: 由于使用了武器，这起盗窃案被认定为加重情节。
senses.why: Law keeps the literal sense: one fact adds weight to another, and the scale of guilt goes up.
senses.whyCN: 法律保留了字面义：一个事实给另一个事实增加重量，罪责的天平随之上升。

senses.title: To intensify a conflict
senses.definition: to make hostility or tension between people or groups stronger
senses.definitionCN: 使人与人、群体与群体之间的敌意或紧张变得更强
senses.example: The speech aggravated the tension between the two groups.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇演讲加剧了两个群体之间的紧张关系。
senses.why: Tension is another kind of load; words can add to it just as weight adds to a cart.
senses.whyCN: 紧张也是一种负荷；言语能像重量压在车上那样，给它再加一层。

senses.title: To make pain sharper
senses.definition: to increase physical pain, especially by movement or pressure on a hurt part
senses.definitionCN: 使身体的疼痛更强，尤因活动或压迫受伤部位
senses.example: Walking up the stairs aggravated the pain in her back.
senses.exampleCN: 上楼梯使她背部的疼痛加剧了。
senses.why: Pain is the most bodily of burdens; anything that presses on it literally adds weight.
senses.whyCN: 疼痛是最身体化的负担；任何压上去的动作都在字面上增加重量。

intro.en: Aggravate is literally 'to add weight', built in Latin from ad- and gravis.
intro.cn: aggravate 字面就是「增加重量」，由拉丁语的 ad- 与 gravis 构成。

items.en: Gravis meant heavy, weighty, or serious, and it also gave English grave, gravity and grief.
items.cn: gravis 意为「沉重的、有分量的、严重的」，也生出英语的 grave、gravity 与 grief。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus gravare 'to weigh down' produced aggravare, to add weight or make heavier.
items.cn: ad-「向」加上 gravare「压重」构成 aggravare，意为「加重、使更沉」。

items.en: The past participle aggravated described something made heavier or more serious.
items.cn: 过去分词 aggravatus 描述被加重、变得更严重的事物。

items.en: English borrowed the word for making a disease or burden worse, the sense that still dominates.
items.cn: 英语借入这个词，用来指使疾病或负担加重，这一含义至今占主导。

items.en: A colloquial sense 'to annoy' appeared later and is often criticised, though it is now widespread.
items.cn: 「使恼火」这一口语义出现较晚，常被批评，但如今已广泛使用。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same-root family; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of making things worse.
note.cn: 形近组收同根词族；近义组收表示「使变糟」的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of making something worse, or a source of annoyance.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「加重；恶化」，也指令人恼火的事。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning making a situation worse or making someone annoyed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「使恶化的；令人恼火的」。

entries.definition: An adjective describing something made worse, or a person who is annoyed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「加重的；被激怒的」。

entries.definition: To become or make something worse in quality or condition.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「恶化；使更糟」，指质量或状况变差。

entries.definition: To make something stronger or more extreme in degree.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「加强；加剧」，指程度变得更强或更极端。

entries.definition: To make a bad situation or feeling even worse.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使恶化；使加剧」，多用于糟糕的局面或情绪。

normalIntro.en: These hooks turn the word into a picture of added weight and rising irritation.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个记忆钩子把词义化成「加重」与「火气上升」的画面。

normal.en: AGGRAVATE hides grave: a grave situation gets heavier.
normal.cn: aggravate 里藏着 grave：严重的局面会变得更沉重。

normal.en: Picture a porter adding one more stone to an already heavy sack.
normal.cn: 想象搬运工往已经很重的袋子里再塞一块石头。

normal.en: A bad knee plus a long walk equals aggravation.
normal.cn: 一只坏膝盖加上一段长路，就是「加重」。

normal.en: When words add weight to a quarrel, they aggravate it.
normal.cn: 当言语给争吵增加重量时，就是把矛盾加剧。

normal.en: Annoyance is weight on the nerves, so the same word serves both senses.
normal.cn: 恼火是压神经上的重量，所以同一个词能兼指两义。

abstract.en: To aggravate is to make the load heavier without adding anything useful.
abstract.cn: 加剧就是在没有增添任何有益之物的情况下，把负荷压得更重。

abstract.en: The word keeps the body's scales even when it speaks of feelings.
abstract.cn: 即便说的是情绪，这个词仍带着身体的天平。

abstract.en: Many problems grow worse because someone keeps pressing on them.
abstract.cn: 许多问题之所以恶化，是因为总有人在上面继续施压。

examples.en: Scratching the rash will only aggravate it.
examples.cn: 抓挠皮疹只会使它更严重。

examples.en: The delay aggravated the anger of the waiting crowd.
examples.cn: 延误使等候人群的怒气更盛。

examples.en: His loud jokes began to aggravate the tired nurses.
examples.cn: 他响亮的笑话开始让疲惫的护士们恼火。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「挨个累」：一件件事挨个累加上去，情况就越来越糟。

sensesIntro.en: The single image of added weight spreads over illness, burdens, temper, law, conflict and physical pain.
sensesIntro.cn: 「增加重量」这一个意象，扩展到病情、负担、脾气、法律、冲突与身体的疼痛。

intro.en: Aggravate sits on the Latin root gravis 'heavy', which also underlies several English words about weight and seriousness.
intro.cn: aggravate 立在拉丁词根 gravis「沉重」上，英语中若干表示重量与严重的词也出自这里。

items.meaning: the act of making worse, or something that annoys
items.meaningCN: 加重；恶化；令人恼火的事
items.example: The extra paperwork was pure aggravation.
items.exampleCN: 额外的文书工作纯粹令人恼火。

items.meaning: making a situation worse or making someone angry
items.example: The aggravating noise continued all night.
items.exampleCN: 那恼人的噪音持续了一整夜。

items.example: The aggravated injury kept him home.
items.exampleCN: 加重的伤势使他只能待在家里。

items.meaning: in a way that annoys or worsens
items.example: He smiled aggravatingly and said nothing.
items.exampleCN: 他恼人地笑了笑，什么也没说。

items.example: The doctor spoke of a grave risk.

items.meaning: the force that pulls things down, or serious importance

items.meaning: to move toward something as if pulled

definition_zh: 总数；合计；骨料；总计的；聚集；合计
definition_en: a total formed from separate parts, or to gather separate things into one whole
core_image: 把散落的一颗颗石子倒进同一个筐里，堆成一整堆
scene: 工地旁，工人把散落的碎石一车车倒进料堆。The workers piled the aggregate beside the road before mixing it with cement.
sceneCN: 这里 aggregate 是「骨料」（第 4 个义项：拌混凝土用的碎石等材料）；句意为工人们把骨料堆在路边，准备与水泥混合。图中可辨识物件：碎石堆、铁锹、水泥袋。

pos.zh: 名词：总数；合计；骨料；聚合体
形容词：总计的；合计的
动词：聚集；合计

derivatives.zh: 由 aggregate 加 -ion 构成，义为「聚集；汇总」
由 aggregate 加 -or 构成，义为「聚合者；信息聚合平台」
由 aggregate 加 -ive 构成，义为「聚合的；聚集性的」

senses.title: A total of separate parts
senses.definition: a total amount formed by adding together several separate amounts or items
senses.definitionCN: 把若干分开的数目或项目相加后得到的总量
senses.example: The aggregate of the three sales figures reached ten thousand.
senses.exampleCN: 三组销售数字合计达到一万。
senses.why: Latin grex meant a flock; aggregare was to drive animals into one herd, and the sum of parts is just such a herd.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 grex 意为「群」；aggregare 是把牲畜赶成一群，而各部分相加的总数正像这样一群。

senses.title: To gather into one group
senses.definition: to bring separate people, things, or data together into a single group
senses.definitionCN: 把分开的人、物或数据聚合成一个整体
senses.example: The small farms aggregate into one large cooperative.
senses.exampleCN: 这些小农场聚合成一个大合作社。
senses.why: The verb keeps the herding image: scattered units are driven into one place.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了「赶成群」的画面：散落的单位被赶到同一个地方。

senses.title: Combined as a whole
senses.definition: describing a figure or measure that is calculated from all the parts together
senses.definitionCN: 形容由全部部分共同算出的数字或尺度
senses.example: The aggregate score decided the winner of the competition.
senses.exampleCN: 总分决定了比赛的胜负。
senses.why: The adjective names the view from above, where individual items blur into one combined number.
senses.whyCN: 形容词指的是从高处看的视角，在那里个别项目模糊成一个合并的数字。

senses.title: Crushed stone for building
senses.definition: sand, gravel, or crushed stone mixed with cement to make concrete
senses.definitionCN: 与水泥混合制成混凝土的砂、砾石或碎石
senses.example: The workers piled the aggregate beside the road before mixing it with cement.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们把骨料堆在路边，准备与水泥混合。
senses.why: A heap of small stones is literally an aggregate: many separate pieces gathered into one mass.
senses.whyCN: 一堆小石子本身就是字面意义上的聚合体：许多分开的碎块聚成一团。

senses.title: A mass of mixed minerals
senses.definition: a rock or mineral mass made of many separate grains or crystals
senses.definitionCN: 由许多分离的颗粒或晶体组成的岩石或矿物块
senses.example: The grey rock is an aggregate of sand and pebbles.
senses.exampleCN: 这块灰色岩石是砂与卵石的聚合体。
senses.why: Geology uses the noun for any body built of distinct grains, the literal flock of stones.
senses.whyCN: 地质学用这个名词指任何由不同颗粒构成的主体，正是石头的「群」。

senses.title: To amount to in total
senses.definition: to add up to a particular total when all parts are counted
senses.definitionCN: 把所有部分计入后达到某个总数
senses.example: Ticket sales aggregated two million last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年门票销售合计达到两百万。
senses.why: When parts are gathered in number, the verb can simply report the figure they make together.
senses.whyCN: 当各部分在数量上被聚拢，动词就可以直接报告它们合起来达到的数字。

senses.title: Totals in economic analysis
senses.definition: a whole-economy measure such as total demand or total output
senses.definitionCN: 用于整体经济的度量，如总需求或总产出
senses.example: Economists watch aggregate demand before setting interest rates.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家在设定利率之前会关注总需求。
senses.why: Economics names the summed economy by the same adjective, treating millions of choices as one flock.
senses.whyCN: 经济学用同一个形容词来指被加总的经济整体，把千百万个选择当成一群。

intro.en: Aggregate goes back to Latin grex, a flock, through the verb for driving animals into one herd.
intro.cn: aggregate 上溯到拉丁语 grex「群」，经由「把牲畜赶成一群」的动词而来。

items.en: Grex meant a flock or herd, the image behind several English words about groups.
items.cn: grex 意为「群、群畜」，是英语中若干表示群体的词的画面来源。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus gregare 'to herd' made aggregare, to drive together into one flock.
items.cn: ad-「向」加上 gregare「赶群」构成 aggregare，意为「赶成一群」。

items.en: The participle aggregatus described things gathered into a single mass.
items.cn: 分词 aggregatus 描述被聚成一体的东西。

items.en: English borrowed the word for a sum of separate items, and later for a heap of stones.
items.cn: 英语借入这个词指分开项目的总和，后来又指一堆石子。

items.en: Building and economics gave the word its technical senses: concrete aggregate and aggregate demand.
items.cn: 建筑与经济学赋予它专业含义：混凝土骨料与总需求。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same-root nouns and adjectives; the near-meaning group gathers words for totals and wholes.
note.cn: 形近组收同根名词与形容词；近义组收表示总数与整体的词。

entries.definition: The noun for the act or result of gathering things into a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「聚集；汇总」，指把事物聚成整体的行为或结果。

entries.definition: A person or service that collects information or offers from many sources.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「聚合者；聚合平台」，指从多方收集信息或商品的人或服务。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning tending to gather things into a group.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「聚合性的；倾向于聚集的」。

entries.definition: The whole amount obtained by adding all the parts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「总数；总额」，指全部部分相加所得的整体。

entries.definition: The result of adding two or more numbers or amounts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「和；总数」，指两个或多个数目相加的结果。

entries.definition: A complete thing made of all its parts together.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「整体；全部」，指由全部部分构成的完整事物。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the word to herds, heaps of stone and the act of adding up.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个记忆钩子把这个词与群、石堆以及加总动作联系起来。

normal.en: AGGREGATE contains 'greg', the Latin word for a flock: many animals driven into one group.
normal.cn: aggregate 里有 greg，拉丁语指「群」：许多动物被赶成一群。

normal.en: Picture a heap of gravel gathered from many small piles.
normal.cn: 想象一堆砾石，是从许多小堆聚拢来的。

normal.en: Think of a scoreboard that adds every game into one aggregate score.
normal.cn: 想一块记分牌，把每场比赛加成一个总分。

normal.en: Concrete is stone plus cement: the stone part is the aggregate.
normal.cn: 混凝土是石子加水泥：石子那部分就是骨料。

normal.en: In the aggregate means 'seen as one heap, not one by one'.
normal.cn: in the aggregate 的意思就是「当成一堆看，而不是一件件看」。

abstract.en: An aggregate hides its parts the way a crowd hides its faces.
abstract.cn: 总量像人群遮住面孔那样，把各个部分遮了起来。

abstract.en: The word begins with animals and ends with economies.
abstract.cn: 这个词从牲畜开始，最后落在经济总量上。

abstract.en: Every total is a decision about which parts to count.
abstract.cn: 每一个总数，都是关于「算进哪些部分」的一次决定。

examples.en: The aggregate of all donations paid for the new clinic.
examples.cn: 所有捐款的合计支付了新诊所的费用。

examples.en: Researchers aggregated data from twenty hospitals.
examples.cn: 研究人员汇总了二十家医院的数据。

examples.en: The team lost on aggregate despite winning the second match.
examples.cn: 尽管赢下第二场比赛，球队仍按总分落败。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「挨个归集」：把东西挨个归到一起，就得到总数。

root: 拉丁语 grex（群）加前缀 ad- 构成 aggregare（赶成一群），过去分词 aggregatus 进入英语，核心是「把分散的部分聚成一个整体」，由此生出「总数」与「骨料」等义。

sensesIntro.en: The word moves from a sum of parts to the act of gathering, then to combined measures, heaps of stone, mineral masses and economic totals.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从各部分之和走到聚集动作，再到合并的度量、石堆、矿物集合体与经济总量。

intro.en: Aggregate belongs to the grex family, whose words all picture groups, herds or gatherings.
intro.cn: aggregate 属于 grex 词族，这一族的词都描绘群体、畜群或聚集。

latinIntro.en: Latin grex gives the base; ad- and -atus build the verb and participle, and English adds -ion, -or, -ive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 grex 提供词基；ad- 与 -atus 造出动词与分词，英语再加 -ion、-or、-ive。

items.meaning: the act or result of gathering into a whole
items.example: The aggregation of small datasets revealed a clear trend.
items.exampleCN: 小数据集的汇总揭示出清晰的趋势。

items.meaning: one that collects things from many sources
items.example: The news aggregator lists stories from many papers.
items.exampleCN: 这个新闻聚合平台列出许多报纸的报道。

items.meaning: tending to gather into a group
items.example: The aggregative habit of the ants protects the colony.
items.exampleCN: 蚂蚁的聚集习性保护了整个群体。

items.example: She is a gregarious host who loves a full room.
items.exampleCN: 她是个爱热闹的主人，喜欢满屋子客人。

items.meaning: to come together in a crowd
items.example: Families congregate in the square each evening.
items.exampleCN: 每到傍晚，各家各户都聚到广场上。

items.meaning: to separate one group from another
items.example: The old rules segregated the students by sex.
items.exampleCN: 旧规矩按性别把学生隔开。

items.meaningCN: 极其恶劣的；令人震惊的
items.example: The report described an egregious error.
items.exampleCN: 报告描述了一处极其严重的错误。

items.meaning: the total demand for goods in an economy
items.example: Aggregate demand fell after the price rise.
items.exampleCN: 价格上涨后总需求下降了。

latinEntries.meaning: to drive together into a flock

definition_zh: 好斗的；有攻击性的；侵略的；积极进取的
definition_en: behaving in a hostile or forceful way, or very determined and energetic
core_image: 向前跨出一步，把拳头伸到别人面前
scene: 两位司机在路口争抢车道，一个人先下车大声指责对方。The aggressive driver shouted and stepped toward the other car.
sceneCN: 这里 aggressive 是「好斗的；有攻击性的」（第 1 个义项：以敌对或强硬的方式对待他人）；句意为这名好斗的司机大喊着朝另一辆车走去。图中可辨识物件：路口、两辆汽车、握紧的拳头。

pos.zh: 形容词：好斗的；有攻击性的；侵略的；积极进取的

collocations.zh: 攻击性行为；好斗的举动

derivatives.zh: 由 aggress- 加 -ion 构成，义为「侵略；攻击性行为」
由 aggress- 加 -or 构成，义为「侵略者；挑衅者」
由 aggressive 加 -ly 构成，义为「咄咄逼人地；积极地」
由 aggressive 加 -ness 构成，义为「好斗；攻击性」

senses.title: Hostile toward others
senses.definition: behaving in a hostile, forceful, or threatening way toward other people
senses.definitionCN: 以敌对、强硬或威胁的方式对待他人
senses.example: The aggressive driver shouted and stepped toward the other car.
senses.exampleCN: 这名好斗的司机大喊着朝另一辆车走去。
senses.why: Latin gradi meant to step; ad- plus gradi made aggredi 'to step toward', and stepping toward someone with force became aggression.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 gradi 意为「迈步」；ad- 加 gradi 构成 aggredi「向……迈步」，带着武力朝人迈步就成了攻击。

senses.title: Invading or warlike
senses.definition: describing a country, army, or act that attacks or seeks to extend power by force
senses.definitionCN: 形容以武力进攻或谋求扩张势力的国家、军队或行为
senses.example: The aggressive army crossed the border at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 这支侵略军在天亮时越过了边界。
senses.why: Nations also step toward one another; when the step crosses a border, the word names outright invasion.
senses.whyCN: 国家之间也会互相迈步；当这一步越过边界，这个词就指赤裸裸的侵略。

senses.title: Boldly enterprising
senses.definition: very determined and energetic in pursuing a goal, often used approvingly in business
senses.definitionCN: 为达成目标而极为坚决、精力充沛，在商业中常带赞许意味
senses.example: The firm's aggressive expansion opened ten new stores in a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司的激进扩张在一年内开了十家新店。
senses.why: The same forward step can be admired instead of feared: energy pushing toward a target is called aggressive.
senses.whyCN: 同样的向前一步，也可以被赞赏而非畏惧：朝目标推进的劲头就被称为积极进取。

senses.title: Forceful in method
senses.definition: applied with great force or pressure, especially in selling, questioning, or negotiating
senses.definitionCN: 以强力或高压方式施行，尤见于推销、提问或谈判
senses.example: Aggressive marketing annoyed many of the older customers.
senses.exampleCN: 强势营销惹恼了不少年长的顾客。
senses.why: A method that pushes its way forward feels like a person stepping into your space, hence the same adjective.
senses.whyCN: 一种硬往前推的方法，感觉就像有人踩进你的地盘，于是用同一个形容词。

senses.title: Fast-spreading, as a disease
senses.definition: describing an illness that grows or spreads quickly and is hard to control
senses.definitionCN: 形容发展或扩散迅速、难以控制的疾病
senses.example: Doctors found an aggressive form of the disease.
senses.exampleCN: 医生发现这是一种侵袭性很强的疾病。
senses.why: Medicine borrowed the image of a force that advances without restraint; a tumour that steps forward fast is aggressive.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用了「不加约束地推进」的画面；迅速向前推进的肿瘤就被称为侵袭性的。

senses.title: Attacking in sport
senses.definition: playing in an attacking style that seeks to score rather than defend
senses.definitionCN: 采取进攻型打法，力求得分而非防守
senses.example: The team played an aggressive second half and scored twice.
senses.exampleCN: 球队下半场踢得极具攻击性，攻入两球。
senses.why: Sport keeps the literal sense: players step toward the opponent's goal, and the style is named for that advance.
senses.whyCN: 体育保留了字面义：球员朝对方球门迈步，这种打法就以这次推进命名。

intro.en: Aggressive is built from Latin gradi 'to step', with the prefix that means 'toward'.
intro.cn: aggressive 由拉丁语 gradi「迈步」加表示「朝向」的前缀构成。

items.en: Gradi meant to step, walk, or go, and it also gave English grade and gradual.
items.cn: gradi 意为「迈步、行走、前进」，也生出英语的 grade 与 gradual。

items.en: Ad- 'toward' plus gradi made aggredi, to step toward something, and often to attack it.
items.cn: ad-「朝向」加 gradi 构成 aggredi，意为「朝某物迈步」，常引申为攻击。

items.en: The participle aggressus described an approach or an attack already begun.
items.cn: 分词 aggressus 描述已经开始逼近或攻击的状态。

items.en: English formed aggressive from the Latin stem, first meaning inclined to attack.
items.cn: 英语由拉丁词干造出 aggressive，最初意为「倾向攻击的」。

items.en: Business and sport added the approving sense of energetic and determined, so the word now cuts both ways.
items.cn: 商业与体育又添了「精力充沛、坚决」的褒义，于是这个词如今正反两用。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same-root nouns; the near-meaning group gathers words of force and confidence.
note.cn: 形近组收同根名词；近义组收表示强势与自信的词。

entries.definition: The noun for hostile behavior or an act of attack.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「侵略；攻击性行为」，指敌对的举动或进攻。

entries.definition: The person or country that starts an attack.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「侵略者；挑衅者」，指发起攻击的人或国家。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning in a forceful or enterprising manner.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「咄咄逼人地；积极地」，指以强硬或进取的方式。

entries.definition: Openly unfriendly or opposed, like an enemy.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「敌对的；怀有敌意的」，像敌人一样公开不友好。

entries.definition: Confident and direct in stating one's views without aggression.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「坚定自信的」，敢于直接表达观点但不带攻击性。

entries.definition: Strong and effective in expression or action.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「强有力的」，指表达或行动有力而有效。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the word to stepping forward, to sales pressure and to a team that keeps attacking.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个记忆钩子把这个词与向前迈步、推销压力以及持续进攻的球队联系起来。

normal.en: AGGREGATE has greg, but AGGRESSIVE has gress: the Latin step.
normal.cn: aggregate 里是 greg，aggressive 里是 gress，后者是拉丁语的「步」。

normal.en: Picture someone stepping toward you with a raised fist.
normal.cn: 想象有人举着拳头朝你迈步而来。

normal.en: An aggressive salesperson follows you down the aisle.
normal.cn: 强势的推销员会一路跟着你走过货架。

normal.en: In business the same word turns into praise: an aggressive plan is a bold plan.
normal.cn: 在商业里同一个词变成褒义：激进计划就是大胆计划。

normal.en: Sport commentators say 'aggressive' when a team keeps pushing forward.
normal.cn: 体育解说员在球队持续前压时会说 aggressive。

abstract.en: Aggression is a step taken across someone else's line.
abstract.cn: 侵犯，就是跨过别人那条线的一步。

abstract.en: The modern word hides its own double edge: drive or threat.
abstract.cn: 这个词把自身的双刃藏了起来：既可以指干劲，也可以指威胁。

abstract.en: A disease can be aggressive because it steps forward faster than treatment.
abstract.cn: 疾病可以很「侵袭」，因为它比治疗推进得更快。

examples.en: The dog became aggressive whenever a stranger approached.
examples.cn: 只要有陌生人靠近，这条狗就变得凶起来。

examples.en: The company adopted an aggressive plan to double its sales.
examples.cn: 公司采取了一项激进计划，要把销售额翻倍。

examples.en: Aggressive questioning made the witness retreat into silence.
examples.cn: 咄咄逼人的提问让证人退入沉默。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「俺哥来势」：俺哥来势汹汹，一副要动手的样子。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（朝向）+ gradi（迈步）构成 aggredi（向……迈步、攻击），其分词 aggressus 进入英语，核心是「带着力度向前逼近」。

sensesIntro.en: The word covers hostile people, invading armies, bold business drive, forceful methods, fast-spreading disease and attacking sport.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词覆盖好斗的人、侵略的军队、大胆的商业冲劲、强硬手法、扩散迅速的疾病与进攻型体育。
