intro.en: Aggressive belongs to the grad- family, words of stepping, grading and graduating.
intro.cn: aggressive 属于 grad- 词族，这一族的词都与迈步、分级、毕业有关。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base grad- means step; prefixes change the direction, and suffixes change the word class.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词基 grad- 意为「步」；前缀改变方向，后缀改变词性。

items.example: The school has a policy against aggression.
items.exampleCN: 学校有禁止攻击行为的规章。

items.meaning: the one who starts an attack
items.example: The aggressor refused to withdraw.
items.exampleCN: 侵略者拒绝撤军。

items.meaning: in a forceful or energetic way
items.example: He argued aggressively for the new plan.
items.exampleCN: 他为新计划激烈辩护。

items.example: The coach praised the team's aggressiveness.
items.exampleCN: 教练称赞了球队的攻击性。

items.example: They agreed on a nonaggressive approach.
items.exampleCN: 他们商定采取非攻击性的做法。

items.meaningCN: 过于强硬的；过度激进的
items.example: The overaggressive sales pitch scared buyers away.
items.exampleCN: 过度强势的推销把买家吓跑了。

items.example: Her passive-aggressive silence said enough.
items.exampleCN: 她那种消极对抗的沉默已说明一切。

items.meaning: a step in rank, or a mark of quality
items.example: She moved up a grade last year.
items.exampleCN: 她去年升了一个年级。

definition_zh: 搅动；摇动；使焦虑；煽动；鼓动
definition_en: to shake or stir something, to make someone anxious, or to campaign publicly for a cause
core_image: 用长柄勺不停搅动一锅浓汤，让沉底的东西翻上来
scene: 厨房里，厨师用长柄勺快速搅动锅里的浓汤。She agitated the soup so the cream would not settle at the bottom.
sceneCN: 这里 agitate 是「搅动」（第 1 个义项：反复摇动或搅拌液体与混合物）；句意为她搅动汤，免得奶油沉在锅底。图中可辨识物件：汤锅、长柄勺、灶台。

pos.zh: 动词：搅动；摇动；使焦虑；煽动

derivatives.zh: 由 agitate 加 -ion 构成，义为「搅动；焦虑；鼓动」
由 agitate 加 -or 构成，义为「搅动器；鼓动者」
由 agitate 加 -ed 构成，义为「焦虑不安的」
由 agitate 加 -ing 构成，义为「令人不安的；搅动的」

senses.title: To stir a liquid
senses.definition: to shake or stir a liquid or mixture so that its parts move and mix
senses.definitionCN: 反复摇动或搅拌液体或混合物，使各部分流动混合
senses.example: She agitated the soup so the cream would not settle.
senses.exampleCN: 她搅动汤，免得奶油沉下去。
senses.why: Latin agitare was the frequentative of agere 'to do, drive', so it meant 'to keep driving something about'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 agitare 是 agere「做、驱动」的反复形式，意为「反复把某物来回驱赶」。

senses.title: To make someone anxious
senses.definition: to disturb someone's calm and make them feel nervous or upset
senses.definitionCN: 打破某人的平静，使其感到紧张或烦躁
senses.example: The strange phone calls agitated her all evening.
senses.exampleCN: 那些奇怪的电话让她整晚心神不宁。
senses.why: If liquid can be stirred, so can the mind: the same word describes thoughts kept from settling.
senses.whyCN: 既然液体能被搅动，心也能被搅动：同一个词描述无法平静下来的思绪。

senses.title: To campaign for a cause
senses.definition: to argue publicly and persistently for a political or social change
senses.definitionCN: 公开而持续地为某项政治或社会变革奔走呼吁
senses.example: The group agitated for cleaner water in the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 这个团体为山谷里更清洁的水源奔走呼吁。
senses.why: Public opinion is another liquid: the campaigner keeps stirring it until it moves.
senses.whyCN: 舆论也是一种液体：鼓动者不断搅动它，直到它流动起来。

senses.title: To stir up debate
senses.definition: to provoke discussion, unrest, or strong feeling among a group
senses.definitionCN: 在一群人中激起讨论、骚动或强烈情绪
senses.example: The question agitated the whole committee for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 这个问题在委员会里激起了数周的争论。
senses.why: A stirred pot does not stay still; a stirred group of people will not either.
senses.whyCN: 被搅动的锅不会静止；被搅动的人群也不会。

senses.title: To shake a container
senses.definition: to shake a vessel or device so that its contents move
senses.definitionCN: 摇动容器或装置，使里面的东西运动
senses.example: Agitate the bottle before pouring the medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 倒药之前先摇匀瓶子。
senses.why: This is the physical core at its simplest: a closed vessel is made to move so its contents follow.
senses.whyCN: 这是最朴素的物理核心：让封闭的容器运动起来，里面的东西随之而动。

intro.en: Agitate is the Latin verb 'to keep driving about', a frequentative built on agere.
intro.cn: agitate 是拉丁语「反复驱动」的动词，由 agere 的反复形式构成。

items.en: Agere meant to do, drive, or set in motion, the base of act, agent and agenda.
items.cn: agere 意为「做、驱动、使运动」，是 act、agent、agenda 的词基。

items.en: The frequentative agitare meant to keep driving or shaking something, to set it in repeated motion.
items.cn: 反复动词 agitare 意为「反复驱动或摇动某物」，使其持续运动。

items.en: The participle agitatus described something shaken or kept in motion, and also a troubled mind.
items.cn: 分词 agitatus 描述被摇动、处于运动中的事物，也指不安的心。

items.en: English borrowed the word first for physical stirring and shaking.
items.cn: 英语最初借入这个词，用来指物理上的搅动与摇动。

items.en: By the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries it also meant to stir up feeling or to campaign politically.
items.cn: 到十八、十九世纪，它又指搅动情绪或在政治上进行鼓动。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same-root family; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of stirring and campaigning.
note.cn: 形近组收同根词族；近义组收表示搅动与鼓动的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for stirring, nervous unrest, or public campaigning.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「搅动；焦躁；鼓动」，兼指物理与情绪、政治三方面。

entries.definition: A device that stirs, or a person who campaigns for change.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「搅拌器；鼓动者」，既指搅动的装置，也指推动变革的人。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning nervous, upset, or physically shaken.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「焦虑不安的；被摇动的」。

entries.definition: To move a spoon or other object around in a liquid.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「搅拌」，指用勺等物在液体中转动。

entries.definition: To interrupt someone's peace or make them worried.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「打扰；使不安」，指打断平静或让人担忧。

entries.definition: To take part in organized activity aimed at a political or social goal.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「开展运动；奔走」，指为政治或社会目标组织活动。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the word to a stirring spoon, a restless mind and a speaker working up a crowd.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个记忆钩子把这个词与搅拌的勺子、不安的心以及煽动人群的演讲者联系起来。

normal.en: AGITATE contains ag- 'do' and -itate, a suffix of repeated action: to keep doing something to a liquid.
normal.cn: agitate 含 ag-「做」与表示反复动作的 -itate：对液体反复做某个动作。

normal.en: Picture a spoon going round and round in a pot of soup.
normal.cn: 想象一把勺子在汤锅里一圈圈地转。

normal.en: A shaken bottle of medicine must be agitated before use.
normal.cn: 药瓶用前要摇匀，这个动作就是 agitate。

normal.en: When worry stirs your thoughts, you feel agitated.
normal.cn: 当忧虑搅动思绪时，你就感到心神不宁。

normal.en: A campaigner agitates public opinion the way a spoon agitates soup.
normal.cn: 鼓动者搅动舆论，就像勺子搅动汤。

abstract.en: To agitate is to refuse to let something settle.
abstract.cn: 搅动，就是不让某样东西沉淀下来。

abstract.en: The same motion calms soup and unsettles people.
abstract.cn: 同一种运动，能让汤均匀，也能让人心不安。

abstract.en: Political agitation is a mind kept deliberately in motion.
abstract.cn: 政治鼓动，就是一颗被有意搅动的心。

examples.en: Agitate the paint before you open the can.
examples.cn: 打开漆罐之前先把它摇匀。

examples.en: The waiting crowd grew agitated as the hours passed.
examples.cn: 随着时间一小时小时过去，等候的人群越来越焦躁。

examples.en: For years the villagers agitated for a new road.
examples.cn: 多年来村民们一直为新修一条路而奔走。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿吉，忒特」：阿吉忒特别，总爱搅动锅里的汤，也搅动大家的情绪。

root: 拉丁语 agere（做、驱动）的反复形式 agitare（反复驱动、摇动），过去分词 agitatus 进入英语，核心意象是「反复搅动」，由物及心，再到政治鼓动。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins with physical stirring, extends to a disturbed mind, and ends with public campaigning and debate.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从物理搅动开始，延伸到被搅乱的心，最后落在公开鼓动与争论上。

branches.en: a liquid stirred in a pot
a closed vessel shaken
a mind kept from settling
opinion stirred for a cause
branches.cn: 为某项事业被搅动的舆论

branches.en: a group stirred into debate

intro.en: Agitate is the frequentative member of the ag- family, marking repeated or vigorous action.
intro.cn: agitate 是 ag- 词族中的反复成员，标记反复或剧烈的动作。

latinIntro.en: Latin agere 'do' plus the frequentative suffix -itare produced agitare, the source of the whole group.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 agere「做」加上反复后缀 -itare 造出 agitare，成为这一组的源头。

items.example: His agitation showed in his shaking hands.
items.exampleCN: 他双手发抖，显出内心的焦躁。

items.meaning: a device or person that stirs
items.example: The washing machine has a central agitator.
items.exampleCN: 这台洗衣机中央有一个搅拌器。

items.example: The agitated patient could not sit still.
items.exampleCN: 焦躁的病人坐立不安。

items.example: It was an agitating piece of news.
items.exampleCN: 那是一条令人不安的消息。

items.example: The leaflet was purely agitational.
items.exampleCN: 这份传单纯粹是鼓动性的。

items.meaning: political art or writing meant to stir support
items.meaningCN: 鼓动宣传；政治宣传作品
items.example: The play was dismissed as agitprop.
items.exampleCN: 这部剧被讥为政治宣传。

items.meaning: in a nervous or shaken manner
items.example: She paced agitatedly by the door.
items.exampleCN: 她在门口焦躁地来回踱步。

items.example: He remained unagitated during the storm.
items.exampleCN: 风暴中他保持平静。

latinEntries.meaning: to do, drive, set in motion

latinEntries.meaningCN: 被摇动的；被搅动的；不安的

definition_zh: 以前；以往；（若干时间）之前
definition_en: before the present time, or before a stated time in the past
core_image: 一条从此刻往回延伸的路，通向已经走远的时刻
scene: 老照片摊在桌上，祖父指着一张泛黄的合影说起往事。He had moved to this town twenty years ago.
sceneCN: 这里 ago 是「以前、以往」（第 1 个义项：从现在往回推算的过去时间）；句意为二十年前他搬到了这个镇子。图中可辨识物件：老照片、相册、台灯。

pos.zh: 副词：以前；以往；（若干时间）之前

derivatives.zh: ago 的古旧变体，义为「过去的；以往的」，今多见于方言与诗歌
由 by 加 gone 构成，与 ago 同出 go 的过去分词，义为「过去的；以往的」

senses.title: Before now in general
senses.definition: at some time in the past, especially a long time before the present
senses.definitionCN: 在过去某个时候，尤指距现在很久以前
senses.example: Long ago, people wrote with quills and ink.
senses.exampleCN: 很久以前，人们用羽毛笔和墨水写字。
senses.why: Old English āgān meant to go away or pass by; whatever has gone is left behind us in time.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 āgān 意为「走开、经过」；凡是走远了的东西，都被留在我们身后的时间里。

senses.title: A measured time before now
senses.definition: used after a length of time to say how far back in the past an event happened
senses.definitionCN: 放在表示时长的词之后，说明某事发生在过去多久以前
senses.example: She moved to the coast three years ago.
senses.exampleCN: 三年前她搬到了海边。
senses.why: The thing that has gone is placed at a measured distance behind the present moment.
senses.whyCN: 已经走远的事，被安放在此刻背后的一个可测量的距离上。

senses.title: In recent-past phrases
senses.definition: in set phrases such as not long ago or a while ago, pointing to the recent past
senses.definitionCN: 用于 not long ago、a while ago 等固定说法，指最近的过去
senses.example: It was not long ago that we last met.
senses.exampleCN: 我们上次见面还是不久前的事。
senses.why: Even a short distance behind now counts as gone; the word measures nearness as well as distance.
senses.whyCN: 即便只是此刻背后很短的一段，也算「已走远」；这个词既量远，也量近。

intro.en: Ago is a native English word, the past participle of an old verb meaning 'to go away'.
intro.cn: ago 是英语本族词，来自一个意为「走开」的古动词的过去分词。

items.en: Āgān meant to go away, pass, or depart, built from ā- 'away' and gān 'to go'.
items.cn: āgān 意为「走开、经过、离去」，由 ā-「离开」与 gān「走」构成。

items.en: The past participle agone meant 'gone by', and it is the direct parent of ago.
items.cn: 过去分词 agone 意为「已经过去的」，正是 ago 的直接来源。

items.en: Middle English shortened agone to ago and kept the sense of time already passed.
items.cn: 中古英语把 agone 缩短为 ago，保留了「已经过去的时间」这一含义。

items.en: The word settled into its fixed place after expressions of time, as in 'two days ago'.
items.cn: 这个词固定在表示时间的说法之后，如 two days ago。

items.en: Ago now works only as an adverb of past time and no longer appears as a participle.
items.cn: 如今 ago 只作表示过去时间的副词，不再以分词形式出现。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words that resemble ago; the near-meaning group gathers other markers of past time.
note.cn: 形近组收与 ago 外形相近的短词；近义组收其他表示过去时间的词。

entries.definition: The sense of one's own identity or self-esteem.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「自我；自尊」，指对自身身份或价值的意识。

entries.definition: An archaic form meaning gone by or past.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，ago 的古旧形式，义为「过去的；以往的」。

entries.definition: A Greek word for a contest or struggle, seen in agony and antagonist.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，希腊语指「竞赛、斗争」，见于 agony 与 antagonist 等词。

entries.definition: At an earlier time than a stated point.
entries.definitionCN: 副词或介词，义为「以前；在……之前」，指早于某个时间点。

entries.definition: At an earlier time, before the present occasion.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「先前；以前」，指在此次之前的时间。

entries.definition: At a time before the one being discussed.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「较早时候」，指所讨论时间之前。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the word to footsteps already taken and to the fixed place it holds after time phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个记忆钩子把这个词与已经走过的脚步以及它在时间短语后的固定位置联系起来。

normal.en: AGO comes from 'gone': what is gone is behind you.
normal.cn: ago 出自「gone」：已经走掉的东西就在你身后。

normal.en: Picture footprints leading back from where you stand now.
normal.cn: 想象一串脚印，从你此刻站立的地方往回延伸。

normal.en: Ago always follows the time: 'three years ago', never 'ago three years'.
normal.cn: ago 总跟在时间后面：three years ago，而不是反过来。

normal.en: Long ago sounds like a fairy-tale opening, which makes the past easy to picture.
normal.cn: long ago 听起来像童话的开头，过去也就容易想象了。

normal.en: The word has no endings: it never becomes agoes or agoed.
normal.cn: 这个词没有词形变化，不会变成 agoes 或 agoed。

abstract.en: Ago is distance measured backward from the speaking voice.
abstract.cn: ago 是从说话者所在之处往回量的距离。

abstract.en: What has gone is not lost; it is simply placed behind the present.
abstract.cn: 已经走掉的并未消失，只是被放在了现在的后面。

abstract.en: The word turns motion into time: to go away becomes to be past.
abstract.cn: 这个词把运动变成时间：走开，就成了过去。

examples.en: She moved to the coast three years ago.
examples.cn: 三年前她搬到了海边。

examples.en: Long ago, this valley was covered by a lake.
examples.cn: 很久以前，这片山谷被一个湖覆盖着。

examples.en: It was not long ago that we last met.
examples.cn: 我们上次见面还是不久前的事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「啊，够」：啊，够了，这些事都是很久以前的了。

root: 古英语 āgān（走开、离去）的过去分词 agone 缩短为 ago，本义「已经走过去的」，引申为「以前、以往」，是本族语词而非拉丁借词。

sensesIntro.en: The word marks general past time, a measured distance before now, and the recent past in set phrases.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词标记泛指的过去、距现在若干时间的过去，以及固定说法中的近过去。

branches.en: a vague long-past time
a measured distance before now
branches.cn: 距现在若干时间的过去

branches.en: the recent past in set phrases
the past viewed as a road back
branches.cn: 把过去看作一条回头的路

branches.en: near and far measured alike

intro.en: Ago has no endings of its own; its 'affixes' are the time words and fixed phrases it joins.
intro.cn: ago 本身没有词缀，它的「构词」体现在与时间词及固定短语的组合。

latinIntro.en: Ago is native English from Old English āgān, so it has no Latin family; this list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: ago 是出自古英语 āgān 的本族语词，没有拉丁语同族词，因此这一项留空。

items.example: Long ago, the village had no bridge.
items.exampleCN: 很久以前，这个村子没有桥。

items.example: They met years ago at a wedding.
items.exampleCN: 他们多年前在一场婚礼上相识。

items.example: Not long ago the shop moved across the street.
items.exampleCN: 不久前这家店搬到了街对面。

items.meaning: a very long time before now
items.example: Ages ago this plain was under the sea.
items.exampleCN: 很久很久以前，这片平原还在海底。

items.example: A while ago I heard a strange noise.
items.exampleCN: 刚才我听到一阵奇怪的声响。

items.example: In agone days the road was empty.
items.exampleCN: 在往昔的日子里，这条路人迹罕至。

items.example: The museum keeps bygone tools and toys.
items.exampleCN: 博物馆收藏着过去的工具与玩具。

items.example: The train was already gone.
items.exampleCN: 火车已经开走了。

definition_zh: 极度痛苦；苦恼；（临死前的）挣扎
definition_en: extreme physical or mental pain, or the final struggle before death
core_image: 一个人蜷缩在地，痛得说不出话
scene: 急诊室外，伤者的家属抱头蹲在走廊里。The agony on his face silenced everyone in the room.
sceneCN: 这里 agony 是「极度痛苦」（第 1 个义项：身体上剧烈的疼痛）；句意为他脸上的痛苦让屋里所有人都沉默了。图中可辨识物件：急诊走廊、病床、家属。

pos.zh: 名词：极度痛苦；苦恼；临死挣扎

collocations.zh: 知心姐姐；答读者问专栏作家

derivatives.zh: 由 agon 加 -ize 构成，义为「使极度痛苦；苦苦思索」
由 agonize 加 -ing 构成，义为「令人极度痛苦的」
由 agonize 加 -ed 构成，义为「痛苦的；显得痛苦的」

senses.title: Extreme physical pain
senses.definition: very severe pain in the body, such as that of a serious injury or illness
senses.definitionCN: 身体上极为剧烈的疼痛，如重伤或重病所带来的
senses.example: The agony on his face silenced everyone in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 他脸上的痛苦让屋里所有人都沉默了。
senses.why: Greek agōn was a contest or struggle; agony is the body fighting a losing battle against pain.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 agōn 指「竞赛、搏斗」；agony 就是身体在与疼痛打一场必败的仗。

senses.title: Mental torment
senses.definition: very great emotional suffering, especially while waiting or fearing something
senses.definitionCN: 极度的情感痛苦，尤见于等待或恐惧某事之时
senses.example: She endured the agony of waiting for the test results.
senses.exampleCN: 她忍受着等待检查结果的精神折磨。
senses.why: The struggle can be fought in the mind alone; no wound is needed for the word to apply.
senses.whyCN: 这场搏斗也能只在心里进行；不需要伤口，这个词同样适用。

senses.title: The struggle before death
senses.definition: the violent final struggle of a dying person or animal
senses.definitionCN: 人或动物临死时剧烈的最后挣扎
senses.example: The wounded bird lay in its death agony.
senses.exampleCN: 受伤的鸟在临死的挣扎中躺着。
senses.why: This is the oldest and most physical sense: life itself is the contest being lost.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老、最身体化的义项：生命本身成了那场输掉的搏斗。

senses.title: A painful ordeal
senses.definition: an experience that is extremely difficult or unpleasant to go through
senses.definitionCN: 一段极其艰难或令人难受的经历
senses.example: The final exam was agony from the first minute.
senses.exampleCN: 期末考试从第一分钟起就是煎熬。
senses.why: Everyday speech stretches the word from a wound to any experience that feels like one.
senses.whyCN: 日常口语把这个词从伤口延伸到任何感觉像伤口的经历。

senses.title: A hard final effort
senses.definition: an intense, exhausting struggle or effort, especially at the end of something
senses.definitionCN: 强烈而耗竭的挣扎或努力，尤指某事接近尾声时
senses.example: The last kilometer of the race was pure agony.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛最后一公里纯粹是苦撑。
senses.why: Any contest has its last stretch, where effort becomes pain; the word names that stretch.
senses.whyCN: 任何竞赛都有最后一段，努力在那里变成疼痛；这个词就指那一段。

intro.en: Agony comes from the Greek word for a contest, then for the struggle of the dying.
intro.cn: agony 出自希腊语表示「竞赛」的词，随后指临死时的挣扎。

items.en: Agōn meant an athletic contest, a struggle, or a trial, with the sense of a fight for victory.
items.cn: agōn 意为「竞技、搏斗、考验」，带有为胜利而战的意思。

items.en: Agōnia named the struggle itself, especially the last struggle of a dying person.
items.cn: agōnia 指搏斗本身，尤指临死之人的最后挣扎。

items.en: Latin borrowed agōnia with the same sense of severe pain or death struggle.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 agōnia，仍指剧痛或临死的挣扎。

items.en: English took the word through French and used it first for the pain of dying.
items.cn: 英语经由法语借入这个词，最初用于指死亡的痛苦。

items.en: The sense widened to any extreme pain, mental or physical, and to painful experiences.
items.cn: 词义扩展到任何极度的身心痛苦，以及令人难受的经历。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same-root verbs and adjectives; the near-meaning group gathers words for severe suffering.
note.cn: 形近组收同根动词与形容词；近义组收表示剧烈痛苦的词。

entries.definition: To suffer or cause great pain, or to struggle painfully with a decision.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「极度痛苦；苦苦思索」，也指使人痛苦。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning causing extreme pain or anxiety.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人极度痛苦的；令人焦虑的」。

entries.definition: An adjective describing a face or cry that shows great pain.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「痛苦的」，形容显出极大痛苦的面容或叫声。

entries.definition: A feeling of physical hurt caused by injury or illness.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「疼痛」，指伤病引起的身体痛感。

entries.definition: Great suffering of the mind, often caused deliberately.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「折磨；煎熬」，多指精神上被施加的痛苦。

entries.definition: The state of experiencing pain, illness, or hardship.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「苦难；痛苦」，指经历疼痛、疾病或艰难的境况。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the word to Greek contests, doomed struggles and the look of a face in pain.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个记忆钩子把这个词与希腊竞赛、必败的挣扎以及痛苦的面容联系起来。

normal.en: AGONY begins with agon, the Greek word for a contest.
normal.cn: agony 开头是 agon，希腊语指「竞赛」。

normal.en: Picture a runner who has lost the final and cannot stand up.
normal.cn: 想象一名输掉决赛、站不起来的赛跑者。

normal.en: The ending -y turns the struggle into a state you are in.
normal.cn: 词尾 -y 把搏斗变成一个你所处的状态。

normal.en: Agony and agonize share the same ache, one as a noun and one as a verb.
normal.cn: agony 与 agonize 共享同一种疼痛，一个作名词，一个作动词。

normal.en: A long queue at the dentist is a familiar picture of agony.
normal.cn: 牙医诊所前的长队是常见的「煎熬」画面。

abstract.en: Agony is a battle with no enemy but pain itself.
abstract.cn: 极度痛苦是一场没有敌人、只有疼痛本身的仗。

abstract.en: The Greeks saw life as a contest, and the word kept that vision.
abstract.cn: 希腊人把生命看作竞赛，这个词保留了这个图景。

abstract.en: Waiting often hurts more than the news being waited for.
abstract.cn: 等待往往比等到的消息更折磨人。

examples.en: He fell to his knees in agony.
examples.cn: 他痛苦地跪倒在地。

examples.en: The agony of not knowing lasted for weeks.
examples.cn: 不知结果的煎熬持续了数周。

examples.en: She described the climb as hours of agony.
examples.cn: 她把那次攀登形容为长达数小时的苦撑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「啊，哥你」：啊，哥你疼得脸都变形了，真是极度的痛苦。

root: 希腊语 agōn（竞赛、搏斗）生出 agōnia（挣扎、临死的痛苦），经拉丁语与法语进入英语，核心是「与疼痛进行一场搏斗」。

sensesIntro.en: The word runs from bodily torment to mental anguish, the death struggle, painful ordeals and the final exhausting effort.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从身体的剧痛走到精神的折磨、临死的挣扎、难熬的经历以及最后耗尽气力的苦撑。

branches.en: the body fighting severe pain
the mind fighting fear and waiting
life losing its final contest
branches.cn: 生命输掉最后一场搏斗

branches.en: an experience felt as pain
the last stretch of a hard effort

intro.en: Agony sits on the Greek root agon 'contest', which also shapes agonize and antagonist.
intro.cn: agony 立在希腊词根 agon「竞赛」上，agonize 与 antagonist 也由此而来。

latinIntro.en: The root is Greek rather than Latin; it entered English through Latin and French forms.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词根来自希腊语而非拉丁语，经由拉丁语与法语形式进入英语。

items.meaning: to suffer or cause extreme pain, or struggle over a choice
items.example: He agonized over the letter for an hour.
items.exampleCN: 他为一封信苦苦纠结了一个小时。

items.example: It was an agonizing wait for news.
items.exampleCN: 那是对消息的煎熬等待。

items.example: She let out an agonized cry.
items.exampleCN: 她发出一声痛苦的喊叫。

items.meaning: in a painfully slow or painful way
items.meaningCN: 令人痛苦地；极其缓慢地
items.example: The minutes passed agonizingly slowly.
items.exampleCN: 那几分钟过去得慢得令人痛苦。

items.meaning: a columnist who gives advice to readers
items.meaningCN: 知心姐姐；答读者问专栏作家
items.example: The agony aunt answered three letters that week.
items.exampleCN: 那位知心姐姐那周回了三封信。

items.meaning: a newspaper feature of readers' problems and advice
items.example: He found the advice in the agony column.
items.exampleCN: 他在读者问答专栏里找到了建议。

items.example: The word agon survives mainly in compounds.
items.exampleCN: agon 主要保留在复合词中。

items.meaning: to make someone hostile or opposed
items.example: Do not antagonize the guards.
items.exampleCN: 不要激怒那些守卫。

definition_zh: 同意；赞成；商定；相符；适合；（语法）一致
definition_en: to share the same opinion, to say yes to a proposal, or to be consistent with something
core_image: 两双手握在一起，表示谈妥了、看法一致
scene: 两位合伙人在合同末尾签下名字，然后相视点头。After weeks of talks, they finally agreed on the price.
sceneCN: 这里 agree 是「商定；达成一致」（第 3 个义项：就某事取得一致意见）；句意为经过数周谈判，他们终于就价格达成一致。图中可辨识物件：合同、签字笔、握手的两人。

pos.zh: 动词：同意；赞成；商定；相符；适合

derivatives.zh: 由 agree 加 -ment 构成，义为「协议；同意；一致」
由 agree 加 -able 构成，义为「令人愉快的；愿意同意的」
由 dis- 加 agreement 构成，义为「分歧；不一致」

senses.title: To share someone's opinion
senses.definition: to have the same opinion as another person about something
senses.definitionCN: 在某事上与另一个人持有相同的看法
senses.example: I agree with you on this point.
senses.exampleCN: 在这一点上我同意你的看法。
senses.why: Latin ad gratum meant 'to one's liking'; to agree is to find another's view pleasing enough to accept it as your own.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ad gratum 意为「合某人的意」；同意，就是觉得别人的看法够合心意，于是当作自己的看法接受下来。

senses.title: To say yes to a proposal
senses.definition: to accept a suggestion, request, or arrangement that has been put to you
senses.definitionCN: 接受别人提出的建议、请求或安排
senses.example: She agreed to the plan at once.
senses.exampleCN: 她立刻赞成了这个计划。
senses.why: Saying yes is the practical face of being of one mind with the person who proposed it.
senses.whyCN: 说「好」是与提议者心意相通的实际表现。

senses.title: To reach a settlement
senses.definition: to come to a shared decision, especially after discussion or bargaining
senses.definitionCN: 经过讨论或讨价还价后作出共同的决定
senses.example: After weeks of talks, they agreed on the price.
senses.exampleCN: 经过数周谈判，他们终于就价格达成一致。
senses.why: Two parties give up a little until one figure pleases both; the pleasing figure is what they agree on.
senses.whyCN: 双方各让一步，直到某个数字让两边都满意；这个让人满意的数字就是他们商定的内容。

senses.title: To match the facts
senses.definition: to be consistent with another account, fact, or record
senses.definitionCN: 与另一种说法、事实或记录相吻合
senses.example: His story does not agree with the facts.
senses.exampleCN: 他的说法与事实不符。
senses.why: Things as well as people can be of one mind: a report that matches the facts is said to agree with them.
senses.whyCN: 不只是人可以心意相通：一份与事实吻合的报告，也被说成与事实相符。

senses.title: To suit the body
senses.definition: to have a good effect on someone's health or comfort, especially food or climate
senses.definitionCN: 对某人的健康或舒适产生良好影响，尤指食物或气候
senses.example: The cold mountain air does not agree with her.
senses.exampleCN: 山里的冷空气不适合她。
senses.why: What suits you is pleasing to you; the old sense of 'pleasing' survives in this bodily use.
senses.whyCN: 适合你的东西必是合你心意的；「合意」这个旧义就残留在这种身体化的用法里。

senses.title: To match in grammar
senses.definition: to have the same number, person, or gender as another word in a sentence
senses.definitionCN: 在句中与另一个词在数、人称或性上保持一致
senses.example: The verb must agree with its subject in number.
senses.exampleCN: 动词必须在数上与主语保持一致。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the social image: two words that fit together are said to be in agreement.
senses.whyCN: 语法借用了社交的画面：两个彼此契合的词，就被说成「一致」。

intro.en: Agree began as a word about pleasing, then moved to sharing a view and matching.
intro.cn: agree 最初是关于「合意、讨喜」的词，后来转向「看法相同」与「彼此吻合」。

items.en: Gratus meant pleasing, welcome, or thankful, the source of gratitude as well.
items.cn: gratus 意为「令人愉快的、受欢迎的、感激的」，也是 gratitude 的来源。

items.en: The phrase ad gratum meant 'according to what pleases', hence 'to one's liking'.
items.cn: 短语 ad gratum 意为「依照所喜欢者」，即「合某人的意」。

items.en: Old French agreer meant to please or to be agreeable to someone.
items.cn: 古法语 agreer 意为「使高兴、讨某人喜欢」。

items.en: English first used agree in the sense of pleasing or satisfying, then for consenting.
items.cn: 英语最初用 agree 表示「使满意」，随后才表示「同意」。

items.en: The modern sense 'to be of one mind' became established in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 「意见一致」这一现代义在十六世纪确立下来。

items.en: The word widened again to matching facts, suiting the body, and grammatical concord.
items.cn: 词义再度扩展，用于事实相符、身体适应以及语法一致。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on agree; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of consent.
note.cn: 形近组收由 agree 构成的词；近义组收表示同意的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for consent, harmony, or a formal arrangement between parties.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「同意；一致；协议」，指双方的一致或正式约定。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning pleasant, or willing to agree.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人愉快的；愿意同意的」。

entries.definition: An adjective or interjection meaning settled by consent.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或感叹词，义为「已商定的；就这么说定了」。

entries.definition: To give permission for something to happen.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「同意；准许」，指允许某事发生。

entries.definition: To agree with an opinion or decision, especially formally.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「同意；赞同」，尤指正式地表示意见相同。

entries.definition: To express approval or agreement, often after consideration.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「同意；赞成」，常指经过考虑后的认可。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the word to pleasing, nodding and the grammar rule of matching forms.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个记忆钩子把这个词与「合意」、点头以及语法上的形式匹配联系起来。

normal.en: AGREE contains 'gree', close to 'grateful': both come from the Latin word for pleasing.
normal.cn: agree 中有 gree，接近 grateful：两者都出自拉丁语表示「讨喜」的词。

normal.en: Picture two people nodding at exactly the same moment.
normal.cn: 想象两个人同时点头，动作完全一样。

normal.en: Agree with a person, agree on a matter, agree to a plan: three little prepositions to remember.
normal.cn: agree with 某人，agree on 某事，agree to 某计划：记住这三个小介词。

normal.en: A contract begins as agreement: two minds made to fit.
normal.cn: 合同源于 agreement：两个心思被调成契合。

normal.en: When a verb agrees with its subject, the sentence's parts nod to each other.
normal.cn: 当动词与主语一致时，句子的各部分就在互相点头。

abstract.en: To agree is first to be pleased, then to be of one mind.
abstract.cn: 同意，先是觉得合意，然后才是心意相同。

abstract.en: The word quietly links feelings to contracts.
abstract.cn: 这个词把感受与契约悄悄连在一起。

abstract.en: Agreement is not the absence of difference but a place where differences meet.
abstract.cn: 一致并非没有分歧，而是分歧相遇的地方。

examples.en: I agree with you on this point.
examples.cn: 在这一点上我同意你的看法。

examples.en: They agreed to meet at noon by the fountain.
examples.cn: 他们约定中午在喷泉旁见面。

examples.en: Her account does not agree with the facts.
examples.cn: 她的说法与事实不符。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「啊，格瑞」：啊，格瑞点头说好，就是同意。

root: 拉丁语 gratus（令人愉快的、感激的）经短语 ad gratum「合意」进入古法语 agreer，再入英语；由「讨人喜欢」引申为「同意」，再扩展为「相符、适合、语法一致」。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts with sharing an opinion, moves to accepting proposals and settling terms, then to matching facts, suiting health and grammar.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从看法相同开始，走到接受提议、商定条件，再到事实相符、身体适应与语法一致。

branches.cn: 双方在一个数字上会合

intro.en: Agree forms a small but busy family of nouns, adjectives and their opposites.
intro.cn: agree 组成一个不大却活跃的词族，包括名词、形容词及其反义词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base gratus 'pleasing' underlies agree, grateful and gratitude alike.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词基 gratus「讨喜的」同时支撑着 agree、grateful 与 gratitude。

items.example: The two firms signed an agreement.
items.exampleCN: 两家公司签署了一份协议。

items.meaningCN: 令人愉快的；愿意同意的
items.example: The terms were agreeable to both sides.
items.exampleCN: 这些条件双方都能接受。

items.example: The evening passed agreeably.
items.exampleCN: 那个夜晚过得很愉快。

items.example: They followed the agreed plan.
items.exampleCN: 他们按已商定的计划行事。

items.example: The experts disagree about the cause.
items.exampleCN: 专家们对原因意见不一。

items.example: The disagreement was settled quietly.
items.exampleCN: 分歧被悄悄解决了。

items.example: Her agreeableness made the work easier.
items.exampleCN: 她的随和让工作轻松了许多。

items.meaning: to accept that opinions differ and stop arguing
items.example: They agreed to disagree and moved on.
items.exampleCN: 他们同意保留分歧，继续往下谈。

definition_zh: 令人愉快的；宜人的；和蔼可亲的；赞同的；可接受的
definition_en: pleasant and enjoyable, or willing to accept something
core_image: 一阵让人愿意点头的微风，既不刺人也不沉闷
scene: 午后的小院里，微风穿过树荫，茶香淡淡地散开。The weather was unusually agreeable for a long walk.
sceneCN: 这里 agreeable 是「宜人的」（第 1 个义项：令人感到舒适愉快的）；句意为这样的天气对长途散步来说格外宜人。图中可辨识物件：小院、树荫、茶杯。

pos.zh: 形容词：令人愉快的；宜人的；赞同的；可接受的

derivatives.zh: 由 agreeable 加 -ly 构成，义为「愉快地；令人愉快地」
由 agreeable 加 -ness 构成，义为「宜人；随和」
由 dis- 加 agreeable 构成，义为「令人不快的；难相处的」

senses.title: Pleasant in weather or setting
senses.definition: pleasantly mild and comfortable, especially of weather or a place
senses.definitionCN: 温和舒适、令人惬意的，尤指天气或场所
senses.example: The weather was unusually agreeable for a long walk.
senses.exampleCN: 这样的天气对长途散步来说格外宜人。
senses.why: Agreeable comes from 'pleasing'; a climate that pleases the body is agreeable in the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: agreeable 出自「讨喜」；让身体感到舒服的气候，就是最古老意义上的 agreeable。

senses.title: Easy to be with
senses.definition: friendly and easy to get along with, so that others enjoy one's company
senses.definitionCN: 友善随和、容易相处，别人乐于与之相伴
senses.example: She has an agreeable manner that puts guests at ease.
senses.exampleCN: 她举止和蔼可亲，让客人感到自在。
senses.why: A person who pleases others is agreeable; the word moves from air and food to manners.
senses.whyCN: 讨人喜欢的人就是 agreeable；这个词从空气与食物转移到了举止。

senses.title: Willing to accept
senses.definition: willing to agree to a suggestion or arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 愿意同意某项建议或安排
senses.example: They were agreeable to a short delay.
senses.exampleCN: 他们愿意接受短暂的延期。
senses.why: What is agreeable finds favor with you; to be agreeable to a plan is to let it find favor.
senses.whyCN: 合意之物会在你这里得到认可；对一项计划 be agreeable，就是让它获得认可。

senses.title: Acceptable as terms
senses.titleCN: 可接受的；合意的（条件、方案）
senses.definition: satisfactory enough for all concerned to accept, as of terms or a compromise
senses.definitionCN: 足够令人满意、各方都能接受，如条件或折中方案
senses.example: The two sides reached a mutually agreeable compromise.
senses.exampleCN: 双方达成了彼此都能接受的折中方案。
senses.why: In bargaining, what pleases both parties is exactly the agreeable solution.
senses.whyCN: 在谈判中，让双方都满意的东西，正是一项「合意」的解决办法。

senses.title: A welcome experience
senses.definition: giving pleasure or satisfaction, as of an experience, surprise, or piece of news
senses.definitionCN: 带来愉悦或满足，如一段经历、一个惊喜或一条消息
senses.example: An agreeable surprise awaited them at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 门口有一个令人愉快的惊喜等着他们。
senses.why: Anything that arrives welcome and pleasing earns the same adjective, whether weather, person or news.
senses.whyCN: 任何到来时受欢迎、令人愉悦的东西，都得到同一个形容词，无论是天气、人还是消息。

intro.en: Agreeable is the adjective of 'pleasing', built from the same Latin root as agree.
intro.cn: agreeable 是「讨喜」的形容词，与 agree 出自同一个拉丁词根。

items.en: Gratus meant pleasing or welcome, and it also gave grateful and gratitude.
items.cn: gratus 意为「令人愉快的、受欢迎的」，也生出 grateful 与 gratitude。

items.en: Ad gratum meant 'to one's liking', the phrase behind the whole agree family.
items.cn: ad gratum 意为「合某人的意」，是整个 agree 词族背后的短语。

items.en: Old French agreable described something pleasing or acceptable to a person.
items.cn: 古法语 agreable 形容令人满意、可以接受的事物。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective for weather, manners, and things that find favor.
items.cn: 英语借入这个形容词，用来形容天气、举止以及讨人喜欢的事物。

items.en: The sense of 'willing to agree' became common in the phrase be agreeable to.
items.cn: 「愿意同意」之义在 be agreeable to 这一说法中变得常见。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the agree family; the near-meaning group gathers words for what pleases or suits.
note.cn: 形近组收 agree 词族；近义组收表示讨喜与适宜的词。

entries.definition: To share an opinion or accept a proposal.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「同意；赞成」，指看法相同或接受提议。

entries.definition: The noun for consent, harmony, or a formal arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「同意；一致；协议」。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning in a pleasant way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「愉快地；令人愉快地」。

entries.definition: Giving a feeling of enjoyment or satisfaction.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人愉快的」，指带来享受或满足感。

entries.definition: Friendly and pleasant in disposition, easy to like.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「和蔼可亲的」，指性情友善、容易让人喜欢。

entries.definition: Satisfactory enough to be allowed or agreed to.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可接受的」，指足以被允许或同意。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the word to the suffix 'can be', to pleasant weather and to a guest one would invite again.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个记忆钩子把这个词与表示「能够」的词尾、宜人的天气以及愿意再请一次的客人联系起来。

normal.en: AGREEABLE holds agree: anything you can agree to is pleasing.
normal.cn: agreeable 里藏着 agree：你能接受的东西，必是合意的。

normal.en: The suffix -able means 'can be', so agreeable is 'can be agreed with'.
normal.cn: 后缀 -able 意为「能够」，所以 agreeable 就是「能够与之合意的」。

normal.en: Picture a mild afternoon that makes everyone nod in comfort.
normal.cn: 想象一个温和的午后，人人都舒服得点头。

normal.en: An agreeable guest is one you would gladly invite a second time.
normal.cn: agreeable 的客人，是你乐意再请一次的人。

normal.en: Weather, manners and terms can all be agreeable: the word fits whatever pleases.
normal.cn: 天气、举止、条件都可以是 agreeable：凡是合意的，这个词都用得上。

abstract.en: To be agreeable is to make room for others to agree.
abstract.cn: 令人愉快，就是给别人留出同意的空间。

abstract.en: The word joins comfort of body to ease of company.
abstract.cn: 这个词把身体的舒适与人际的自在连在一起。

abstract.en: A compromise becomes agreeable when both sides can breathe.
abstract.cn: 当双方都能松一口气时，折中方案才变得合意。

examples.en: The weather was unusually agreeable for a long walk.
examples.cn: 这样的天气对长途散步来说格外宜人。

examples.en: She has an agreeable manner that puts guests at ease.
examples.cn: 她举止和蔼可亲，让客人感到自在。

examples.en: They were agreeable to a short delay.
examples.cn: 他们愿意接受短暂的延期。

items.meaning: in a pleasant or willing manner

items.example: Her agreeableness made the work easier.

items.meaning: unpleasant or hard to get along with

items.example: He spoke disagreeably to the clerk.
items.exampleCN: 他没好气地对店员说话。

items.meaning: to share an opinion or accept

items.exampleCN: 你同意这个计划吗？

items.example: The two experts disagree.

items.meaning: the tendency to be pleasing and easy to agree with
items.example: His agreeability won over the whole team.
items.exampleCN: 他的随和赢得了整个团队。
